# GoodAIPromt: full prompt library

A free AI prompt library for ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Midjourney and AI video tools. Fill in the blanks, copy the prompt, get better answers. New prompts daily.

Placeholders in [SQUARE BRACKETS] are for the user's own details. Source: https://goodaipromt.com/

---

## Affiliate program plan and partner recruitment

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/affiliate-program-plan/
Category: Marketing
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-21

Design an affiliate program — commission model, terms, partner profile and recruitment emails — that attracts promoters who fit your brand.

Prompt:

You are an affiliate marketing manager. Design an affiliate program for my business.

What we sell, average order value and gross margin: [PRODUCT, AOV, MARGIN]
Customer lifetime value or repeat purchase rate (if known): [LTV OR REPEAT RATE]
Who our customers follow or read (creators, blogs, newsletters, communities): [INFLUENCES]
Tools we use or plan to use for tracking: [TRACKING TOOL]
Brand rules partners must follow: [BRAND RULES]

Create:
1. Commission options (percentage, flat fee, tiered, recurring) with the maths for my margin, and a recommendation.
2. Key terms: cookie window, payout threshold and schedule, what doesn't count (refunds, coupon sites, brand-name ads), and disclosure requirements.
3. An ideal affiliate profile and 5 types of partners to recruit first.
4. A recruitment email and a shorter DM version.
5. An affiliate welcome kit outline: product info, key messages, approved claims, assets, dos and don'ts.
6. A 90-day launch plan and the metrics to judge success.

Make sure affiliates are required to disclose the relationship. Do not promise earnings to partners.

## AI music video scene prompt

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/ai-music-video-scene/
Category: Video
Works with: Veo, Kling, Runway and Seedance
Published: 2026-11-21

Plan and generate atmospheric music video shots that match a song's mood, tempo and lyrics, with consistent visuals across clips.

Prompt:

You are a music video director. Plan AI-generated shots for my song.

Song title, genre and tempo (BPM if known): [SONG DETAILS]
Mood and main themes: [MOOD AND THEMES]
Key lyric lines or images: [LYRICS OR IMAGES]
Artist appearance (if they appear): [ARTIST DESCRIPTION OR "NO ARTIST"]
Format: [ASPECT RATIO, E.G. 16:9 OR 9:16]

Create:
1. A visual world in 5 lines: locations, colour palette, light, wardrobe, recurring symbol.
2. A shot list of 10 shots of 4–8 seconds each, matched to song sections (intro, verse, chorus, bridge, outro). For each: section, shot description, camera movement, speed (slow motion, real time), and how it relates to the lyrics.
3. A ready-to-paste video prompt for each shot, repeating the visual world details so clips stay consistent, and ending with "no text, no logos".
4. Editing notes: where to cut on the beat and which shots to repeat in the chorus.

Keep camera moves simple (slow dolly, drift, static). Avoid crowds and fast choreography, which AI video handles poorly.

## API documentation from your code

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/api-documentation-from-code/
Category: Coding
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-21

Generate clear API reference docs from route handlers or code — endpoints, parameters, responses, errors and examples — ready for developers.

Prompt:

You are a technical writer for developer tools. Write API reference documentation from this code.

API purpose and audience: [API PURPOSE AND USERS]
Base URL and authentication method: [BASE URL AND AUTH]
Framework and language: [FRAMEWORK]
Code (routes, handlers, schemas, validation):
[CODE]

For each endpoint write:
1. Method, path and a one-line description of what it does.
2. Authentication and permissions required.
3. Path, query and body parameters in a table: name, type, required, description, constraints and defaults.
4. Example request (curl) and example success response (JSON).
5. Error responses: status code, when it happens, example body.
6. Notes: pagination, rate limits, idempotency or side effects, only if visible in the code.

Then add:
- A short getting-started section with an authentication example.
- An OpenAPI 3 YAML snippet for the endpoints.
- A list of behaviours that are unclear from the code (for example, missing validation or undocumented error cases).

Document only what the code shows. Use realistic but obviously fake example values.

## Find the brand archetype that fits your business

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/brand-archetype-finder/
Category: Marketing
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-21

Match your business to one of the 12 brand archetypes and get a voice, visual and messaging direction you can apply this week.

Prompt:

You are a brand strategist. Help me choose a brand archetype for my business and turn it into practical guidelines.

Business and what we sell: [BUSINESS AND PRODUCT]
Ideal customer and what they want to feel: [CUSTOMER AND DESIRED FEELING]
3 competitors and how they come across: [COMPETITORS]
Words customers already use to describe us: [CUSTOMER WORDS]
Words we never want to be associated with: [WORDS TO AVOID]

Do this:
1. Shortlist the 3 archetypes (from the classic 12) that fit best. For each, explain why in 2 sentences, using my inputs.
2. Show which archetypes my competitors seem to use, and where there is room to stand apart.
3. Recommend one primary archetype and, if useful, one secondary. Explain the trade-off.
4. For the chosen archetype, give: 5 voice traits with "we say / we don't say" examples, visual direction (colours, imagery, typography mood), 3 core brand promises, and 3 sample social captions.
5. List 3 ways the archetype could go wrong for my business (for example, sounding preachy or cold) and how to avoid them.

Base every recommendation on my inputs. If something important is missing, ask me before deciding.

## Brand tagline options with a clear promise

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/brand-tagline-ideas/
Category: Marketing
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-21

Generate short tagline options grouped by style, each tied to a real customer benefit, plus a quick test to pick the strongest one.

Prompt:

You are a senior copywriter. Write tagline options for my brand.

Brand and what we sell: [BRAND AND PRODUCT]
Target customer: [CUSTOMER]
The main benefit customers get: [MAIN BENEFIT]
What makes us different from alternatives: [DIFFERENCE]
Brand personality in 3 words: [PERSONALITY]
Taglines of competitors (to avoid sounding similar): [COMPETITOR TAGLINES]

Write:
1. 20 taglines of 2–7 words, in 4 groups: direct benefit, emotional, playful or witty, and bold or provocative.
2. For each, one line on which benefit or difference it expresses.
3. Score the top 8 from 1–5 on clarity, memorability, fit with the personality and difference from competitors. Show a table.
4. Recommend 3 finalists and explain where each would work best (website hero, packaging, ads).
5. Flag any tagline that could make an unprovable claim or sound like a competitor.

Avoid clichés like "quality", "excellence", "solutions" and "your trusted partner".

## Business continuity plan for a small business

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/business-continuity-plan/
Category: Strategy
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-21

Prepare for disruptions like outages, key staff absence or supplier failure with a simple continuity plan, contacts and recovery steps.

Prompt:

You are a business continuity consultant for small businesses. Create a continuity plan for my company.

Business, size and location(s): [BUSINESS]
Critical activities customers depend on: [CRITICAL ACTIVITIES]
Key systems and tools: [SYSTEMS]
Key people and what only they know or can do: [KEY PEOPLE]
Main suppliers and partners: [SUPPLIERS]
Past disruptions or near misses: [PAST INCIDENTS]

Create:
1. A business impact table: each critical activity, how long we can survive without it, and the impact on customers and revenue.
2. The 6 most likely disruption scenarios for my business, with likelihood and impact (low/medium/high).
3. For each scenario: first-hour actions, workaround to keep serving customers, who is responsible, and recovery steps.
4. Single points of failure (people, systems, suppliers) and how to reduce each.
5. A contact sheet template and a customer communication template for a disruption.
6. A plan to test and update the plan twice a year.

Keep it practical, in checklists, and short enough to use under stress.

## Find the moat that protects your business

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/business-moat-analysis/
Category: Strategy
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-21

Assess which competitive advantages your business really has, how easy they are to copy, and what to build next to stay ahead.

Prompt:

You are a strategy consultant. Assess the competitive advantages of my business honestly.

Business, market and customers: [BUSINESS DESCRIPTION]
What we believe makes us different: [CLAIMED STRENGTHS]
Main competitors and what they do well: [COMPETITORS]
Why customers choose us (evidence if any): [CUSTOMER REASONS]
Resources we have (team, data, partnerships, assets): [RESOURCES]

Do this:
1. Test each claimed strength: Do customers value it? Can a competitor copy it in under 12 months? Score each 1–5 on value and difficulty to copy, with reasons.
2. Check each moat type — switching costs, network effects, proprietary data or know-how, brand and trust, cost or scale advantages, regulation or exclusive access — and say whether we have it, could build it, or should ignore it.
3. Name our strongest current advantage and our biggest vulnerability.
4. Recommend one moat to invest in over the next 12 months, with 5 concrete actions and early signs that it is working.
5. List what a well-funded competitor would most likely do to beat us, and how we would respond.

Be direct. If a strength is weak, say so. Do not invent market data.

## Choose the right chart for your data

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/choose-the-right-chart/
Category: Data analysis
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-21

Get a recommended chart type for your data and message, with layout, labels and colour advice — and the charts you should avoid.

Prompt:

You are a data visualisation expert. Recommend the best way to chart my data.

What the data contains (columns, units, time range, number of rows): [DATA DESCRIPTION]
A sample of the data: [SAMPLE ROWS]
The message I want the audience to understand: [KEY MESSAGE]
Audience and where it will be shown (slide, report, dashboard): [AUDIENCE AND FORMAT]
Tool I'll use: [TOOL, E.G. EXCEL, GOOGLE SHEETS, POWER BI]

Do this:
1. Name the type of comparison (change over time, ranking, part-to-whole, distribution, relationship, geography).
2. Recommend the best chart type and one alternative, with reasons.
3. Explain the setup: what goes on each axis, sorting, scale (start at zero or not, and why), and any grouping or filtering.
4. Write a title that states the finding, plus axis labels and one annotation that points to the key insight.
5. Give colour advice: one highlight colour for what matters, grey for the rest, colour-blind friendly.
6. Name charts to avoid for this data and why.
7. Give step-by-step instructions to build it in my tool.

If the message isn't supported by the sample data, tell me.

## Cinematic portrait with dramatic lighting prompt

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/cinematic-portrait-lighting/
Category: Image
Works with: Midjourney, Flux and GPT Image
Published: 2026-11-21

Create moody, film-still portraits by choosing a lighting setup, lens, colour grade and emotion — for posters, covers and characters.

Prompt:

Cinematic portrait of [SUBJECT: AGE, LOOK, CLOTHING], [EXPRESSION AND EMOTION, E.G. QUIET DETERMINATION, EYES SLIGHTLY DOWN], [FRAMING, E.G. TIGHT MEDIUM CLOSE-UP], lit with [LIGHTING SETUP, E.G. REMBRANDT LIGHTING FROM A SINGLE WINDOW ON THE LEFT], motivated by [LIGHT SOURCE, E.G. A STREETLAMP OUTSIDE], deep soft shadows, [BACKGROUND, E.G. DARK APARTMENT WITH BLURRED CITY LIGHTS], shot on [LENS, E.G. 85MM AT F/1.8], shallow depth of field, [COLOUR GRADE, E.G. TEAL AND AMBER], subtle film grain, anamorphic feel, film still from a [GENRE, E.G. NEO-NOIR DRAMA], realistic skin texture

## Competitor pricing research you can act on

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/competitor-pricing-research/
Category: Research
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-21

Organise competitor pricing into a clear comparison table, spot patterns in packaging and value, and see where your price fits.

Prompt:

You are a pricing analyst. Help me analyse competitor pricing.

Our product, plans and prices: [OUR PRICING]
Our target customer: [TARGET CUSTOMER]
Competitor pricing information I collected (copy from their pricing pages, with date checked): [COMPETITOR PRICING DATA]

Do this:
1. Build a comparison table: competitor, plan, price, billing period, main limits (users, usage, features), key add-ons, free trial or free plan.
2. Normalise prices to a comparable unit (for example, per user per month, or per typical customer) and show the calculation.
3. Describe the pricing patterns: value metrics used, common tiers, what is held back for higher plans, discounts.
4. Show where our pricing sits for a typical customer: cheaper, similar or more expensive, and for what difference in value.
5. List 3–5 pricing questions or experiments worth considering, with the reasoning and risks.
6. Note gaps in the data I should fill before deciding.

Use only the data I provided. Do not guess prices that are not listed; mark them as unknown.

## Customer service tone guide for your team

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/customer-service-tone-guide/
Category: Customer service
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-21

Create a support tone-of-voice guide with do and don't examples, phrases for tricky moments and rewrites of your real replies.

Prompt:

You are a customer experience lead. Create a tone of voice guide for our support team.

Company and what we sell: [COMPANY]
Our customers and how they usually feel when they contact us: [CUSTOMERS AND FEELINGS]
Brand personality in 3–4 words: [PERSONALITY]
Support channels (email, chat, phone, social): [CHANNELS]
3–5 real replies from our team (anonymised): [SAMPLE REPLIES]

Create:
1. 4 tone principles, each with a one-line explanation, a "do" example and a "don't" example.
2. How tone should adjust by situation: simple question, bug or outage, angry customer, refund or cancellation, saying no, good news.
3. A phrase bank: openers, apologies that sound sincere, explaining delays, saying no kindly, closing lines. Plus 10 phrases to avoid and better alternatives.
4. Channel notes: length and formality for each channel.
5. Rewrites of my sample replies in the new tone, with a note on what changed.

Keep the guide short enough to read in 10 minutes. Use plain, human language.

## Reply to a GDPR data subject access request

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/data-subject-access-request-reply/
Category: Legal
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-21

Plan and draft a response to a personal data access or deletion request, with a checklist of steps and points to confirm with a lawyer.

Prompt:

You are a privacy operations specialist (not a lawyer). Help me handle a data subject request.

Our company and country/region: [COMPANY AND LOCATION]
Type of request: [ACCESS, DELETION, CORRECTION, OBJECTION, PORTABILITY]
The request as received (remove sensitive details): [REQUEST TEXT]
Date received: [DATE]
Where we store personal data (systems, tools, files): [DATA LOCATIONS]
Anything that may complicate it (legal holds, unpaid invoices, unclear identity): [COMPLICATIONS]

Create:
1. A step-by-step checklist: confirm identity, log the request, find the data in each system, review for third-party information, prepare the response, record what was done.
2. Points to confirm with a qualified adviser, such as response deadlines, possible extensions, exemptions and fees under the law that applies to us. Do not state these as facts.
3. A short acknowledgement email to send now.
4. An identity verification request that asks only for what is needed.
5. A draft final response for this request type, with placeholders such as {DATA CATEGORIES} and {RETENTION PERIOD}.
6. A simple record-keeping template for this and future requests.

Use plain, respectful language. Flag anything that looks like it needs legal review.

## Day-in-the-life documentary-style video prompt

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/day-in-the-life-documentary-video/
Category: Video
Works with: Veo, Kling, Runway and Seedance
Published: 2026-11-21

Create a short documentary-style AI video of a maker, chef or founder at work — handheld feel, natural light and detail shots.

Prompt:

Create a [LENGTH, E.G. 12-SECOND] documentary-style video, [ASPECT, E.G. 16:9].

Person: [PERSON, E.G. CERAMICIST IN HER 50S, CLAY-STAINED APRON, GREY HAIR TIED BACK]
Workplace: [PLACE, E.G. SMALL SUNLIT POTTERY STUDIO WITH SHELVES OF DRYING BOWLS]
Time of day and light: [LIGHT, E.G. EARLY MORNING, SOFT WINDOW LIGHT, DUST IN THE AIR]

Shot 1: wide, the person unlocks the door and switches on the lights, handheld camera.
Shot 2: close-up of hands at work: [MAIN ACTION, E.G. SHAPING A BOWL ON THE WHEEL].
Shot 3: medium shot, concentrated face, slight camera drift.
Shot 4: detail shot of [TOOLS OR MATERIALS], shallow depth of field.
Shot 5: wide, the person steps back to look at the finished [RESULT], gentle smile.

Style: observational documentary, natural colour, slight grain, realistic textures, no music video effects, no text.
Sound: ambient room sound, [SPECIFIC SOUNDS, E.G. THE WHIR OF THE WHEEL].
Avoid: posed looks into the camera, extra people, distorted hands.

## Debate practice partner that argues back

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/debate-practice-partner/
Category: Education
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-21

Practise debating with an AI opponent that presents strong counterarguments, rebuts your points and gives feedback on your reasoning.

Prompt:

You are a skilled debate opponent and coach. Let's practise a debate.

Motion: [MOTION, E.G. "THIS HOUSE WOULD BAN HOMEWORK IN PRIMARY SCHOOLS"]
My side: [FOR OR AGAINST]
My level: [LEVEL, E.G. HIGH SCHOOL, UNIVERSITY, BEGINNER]
Format and time per speech: [FORMAT, E.G. 3 ROUNDS, 200 WORDS EACH]

Rules:
1. Take the opposite side. Start with your opening argument: 3 strong points, each with reasoning and the type of evidence that would support it. Do not invent statistics; describe evidence in general terms.
2. After each of my turns, rebut my strongest point first, then add a new argument.
3. Argue in good faith: no strawmen, and concede points that are clearly correct.
4. After the final round, switch to coach mode and give me: a score from 1–10 for argument strength, rebuttal, evidence and clarity; my best moment; the argument I missed; one logical fallacy or weak spot I used, if any; and 3 tips for next time.

Wait for my reply after each of your turns.

Generate a sheet of matching die-cut stickers with white borders and a consistent style — for merch, packaging inserts and print-on-demand.

COFFEE SHOP MORNINGS], each sticker a separate cute object: [LIST OF OBJECTS OR CHARACTERS], [STYLE, E.G. BOLD KAWAII VECTOR ILLUSTRATION WITH THICK OUTLINES], [COLOUR PALETTE, E.G. WARM BROWNS, CREAM AND PASTEL PINK], flat colours with simple shading, thick white die-cut border around each sticker, even spacing, no overlapping, [OPTIONAL TEXT, E.G. ONE STICKER WITH THE WORDS "BUT FIRST COFFEE"], clean edges, print-ready look

## Email list segmentation plan for better results

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/email-list-segmentation-plan/
Category: Marketing
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-21

Split your email list into useful segments based on behaviour and needs, with a message plan for each so every send feels relevant.

Prompt:

You are an email marketing strategist. Design a segmentation plan for my email list.

Business and what we sell: [BUSINESS]
List size and where subscribers come from: [LIST SIZE AND SOURCES]
Data we have on subscribers (purchases, clicks, signup form fields, tags): [AVAILABLE DATA]
Email tool we use: [EMAIL PLATFORM]
Main goal for email this quarter: [GOAL]

Create:
1. 4–6 segments I can build with my current data. For each: name, rule to define it in plain logic, why it matters, and roughly how to find it in my tool.
2. A message plan per segment: what they need to hear, 3 email ideas, ideal frequency, and the main call to action.
3. One automated flow to set up first, with trigger, emails and timing.
4. Data I should start collecting to improve segments later (one simple signup or preference question).
5. How to measure if segmentation is working: which metrics to compare and over what period.

Keep it practical for a small team. Do not create segments that need data I don't have.

## Executive summary of a long document

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/executive-summary-long-document/
Category: Writing
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-21

Condense a long report, proposal or research document into a one-page executive summary that leads with conclusions and decisions.

Prompt:

You are an experienced business writer. Write an executive summary of the document below.

Who will read it and what they need to decide: [READERS AND DECISION]
Maximum length: [LENGTH, E.G. 300 WORDS OR ONE PAGE]
Document:
[PASTE DOCUMENT]

Write:
1. A one-sentence bottom line: the main conclusion or recommendation.
2. Context: why this matters now, in 2–3 sentences.
3. Key findings: 3–5 bullets, each with the most important supporting figure from the document.
4. Recommendation or ask: what the reader should decide or do, by when, and the cost or resources if stated.
5. Risks and open questions in 2–3 bullets.
6. Next steps.

Lead with conclusions, not background. Use only facts and numbers from the document and keep figures exactly as written. After the summary, list anything important you left out so I can decide if it should go back in.

## Expert interview plan to learn a field fast

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/expert-interview-question-plan/
Category: Research
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-21

Prepare for an interview with a subject matter expert — goals, smart questions, follow-ups and a note template — to get real insight in one hour.

Prompt:

You are a research consultant who interviews experts for a living. Prepare me for an expert interview.

Topic or field: [TOPIC]
What I need to learn and why (decision, project, article): [GOAL]
Expert's background: [EXPERT BACKGROUND]
What I already know: [MY CURRENT KNOWLEDGE]
Interview length: [LENGTH]

Create:
1. 3 learning goals for the interview, ranked.
2. A short opening that explains the purpose and builds rapport.
3. 12–15 questions, grouped by goal and ordered from broad to specific. Include questions about: how decisions are really made, common mistakes, what outsiders misunderstand, recent changes, and how they would approach my situation.
4. Follow-up prompts to get examples and details ("Can you walk me through the last time...").
5. 3 questions to ask only if time allows.
6. A closing: who else I should talk to and what I should read.
7. A note template to fill in during and right after the call.

Mark the 5 must-ask questions. Avoid leading or yes/no questions.

## Read financial statements in plain English

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/financial-statements-plain-english/
Category: Finance
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-21

Understand an income statement, balance sheet and cash flow statement — what each line means, key ratios and the questions to ask.

Prompt:

You are a patient finance teacher. Explain these financial statements to me in plain English.

Company and industry: [COMPANY]
My role and why I'm reading these: [ROLE AND PURPOSE, E.G. OWNER, NEW MANAGER, INVESTOR]
Period covered: [PERIOD]
Statements (paste income statement, balance sheet and cash flow statement, or the ones I have):
[STATEMENTS]

Do this:
1. Explain what each statement shows in 2 sentences, using an everyday analogy.
2. Walk through the main lines of each statement: what they mean and what stands out here.
3. Calculate and explain these ratios where the data allows: gross margin, net margin, current ratio, debt-to-equity, and operating cash flow vs net profit. Show the maths.
4. Explain how profit and cash differ in these numbers, and why.
5. List 3 strengths and 3 concerns, based only on the figures.
6. Give 5 questions to ask the accountant or management.

Use only the numbers provided and keep them exactly as written. Do not give investment advice. Mark anything you cannot judge without more context or previous periods.

## Fitness workout demo video prompt

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/fitness-workout-demo-video/
Category: Video
Works with: Veo, Kling, Runway and Seedance
Published: 2026-11-21

Generate short gym or home workout clips with correct-looking form, clear camera angles and an energetic look for fitness content.

Prompt:

Create a [LENGTH, E.G. 6-SECOND] [ASPECT, E.G. 9:16 VERTICAL] fitness video.

Athlete: [DESCRIPTION, E.G. ATHLETIC MAN IN HIS 20S, BLACK T-SHIRT, GREY SHORTS]
Location: [LOCATION, E.G. MODERN GYM WITH RUBBER FLOOR AND DUMBBELL RACK, OR LIVING ROOM WITH A YOGA MAT]
Exercise: [EXERCISE, E.G. GOBLET SQUAT WITH A KETTLEBELL], performed slowly with controlled form: [KEY FORM CUES, E.G. CHEST UP, KNEES TRACK OVER TOES, HIPS BELOW KNEES]
Reps: [NUMBER] smooth repetitions
Camera: [ANGLE, E.G. 45-DEGREE SIDE VIEW, FULL BODY IN FRAME], tripod-steady, no cuts
Lighting: [LIGHT, E.G. BRIGHT, CLEAN OVERHEAD LIGHT WITH SOFT SHADOWS]
Mood: energetic but realistic, natural sweat, real muscle definition
Avoid: extra limbs, warped equipment, people in the background, on-screen text, unsafe form.

## Fix keyword cannibalization between your pages

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/fix-keyword-cannibalization/
Category: SEO
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-21

Find pages competing for the same keyword and decide whether to merge, redirect, differentiate or re-link them, with a clear action list.

Prompt:

You are a technical SEO consultant. Help me resolve keyword cannibalization on my site.

Site and topic: [SITE]
Query or topic that is affected: [KEYWORD]
Competing pages — for each: URL, title, main purpose, clicks and impressions for the query, backlinks if known, and a short content summary:
[PAGE DATA]
Which page I would like to rank (if I know): [PREFERRED PAGE]

Do this:
1. Confirm whether this is real cannibalization or two pages serving different intents. Explain your reasoning.
2. Choose the page that should own the query, based on intent fit, performance and links.
3. For every other page, recommend one action: merge into the main page and 301 redirect; rewrite to target a different intent and keyword; keep but de-optimise; or noindex. Give the reason.
4. List exact changes: titles, H1s, sections to move, internal links and anchor text to update.
5. Explain how to check the result over the next 4–8 weeks in Search Console.

Do not guess data I didn't provide. If something is missing, say what to check.

## Screener survey to recruit the right interviewees

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/interview-screener-survey/
Category: Research
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-21

Create a short screener survey that filters for the people you actually need for user interviews, without hinting at the right answers.

Prompt:

You are a user research lead. Write a screener survey to recruit participants for interviews.

Research goal: [WHAT WE WANT TO LEARN]
Who we need (behaviours, not just demographics): [TARGET PARTICIPANTS]
Who we must exclude: [EXCLUSIONS, E.G. COMPETITORS' EMPLOYEES, RECENT PARTICIPANTS]
Number of interviews and mix needed: [NUMBER AND QUOTAS]
Where we will share the survey: [CHANNEL]

Create:
1. 8–12 screener questions, mostly multiple choice, that check behaviour (what they did recently) rather than opinions. Include at least one question with a decoy answer to catch people who over-claim.
2. For each question: the answer options, which answers qualify, disqualify or are neutral (in a separate table I keep private).
3. One open-text question that tests if the person can explain things clearly.
4. A scoring rule and quotas so we get the right mix.
5. A short invitation text and a thank-you message for people who don't qualify.

Do not reveal the target profile in the question wording. Keep the survey under 3 minutes.

## Solve math problems step by step with checks

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/math-problems-step-by-step/
Category: Education
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-21

Get a clear step-by-step solution to a math problem, with the reasoning for each step, a final check and a similar problem to practise.

Prompt:

You are a patient maths tutor. Help me solve this problem and understand the method.

Problem: [PASTE THE PROBLEM EXACTLY]
My level or course: [LEVEL, E.G. GRADE 9, UNIVERSITY CALCULUS]
What I have tried so far (if anything): [MY ATTEMPT]

Do this:
1. Restate what the problem is asking and list the given information.
2. Name the method or rule we will use and why it fits.
3. Solve step by step. Number each step and give a one-line reason for it. Show all working; do not skip algebra.
4. Check the answer a different way (substitute it back, estimate, or use units) and say whether it holds.
5. If I shared an attempt, point out exactly where it went wrong, kindly.
6. Give one similar practice problem with the answer hidden at the bottom.

Use simple language for my level. If the problem is ambiguous, ask before solving.

## Write a clear problem statement for a new product

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/product-problem-statement/
Category: Strategy
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-21

Turn a vague product idea into a sharp problem statement — who has the problem, when it happens, what it costs and how you'll know it's solved.

Prompt:

You are an experienced product manager. Help me write a clear problem statement.

My idea or the problem I think exists: [IDEA]
Who I think has this problem: [TARGET USERS]
What I've seen or heard that suggests it is real: [EVIDENCE]
How people deal with it today: [CURRENT ALTERNATIVES]

Do this:
1. Rewrite my idea as a problem statement in this form: "[User] needs a way to [job] when [situation], because [current obstacle], which costs them [time, money, risk or frustration]." Give 3 versions of different scope.

3. List the assumptions behind the statement, ranked by risk.
4. Describe what "solved" looks like: 3 measurable outcomes for the user.
5. Suggest 3 quick ways to validate the riskiest assumption in under two weeks, with what result would change my mind.
6. Write 5 neutral interview questions to test the problem without leading people.

Constraints (budget, hosting, compliance, deadlines): [CONSTRAINTS]
Integrations needed: [THIRD-PARTY SERVICES]

Before proposing anything, list any questions whose answers would change the design, and state the assumptions you will use.

Then provide:
1. The simplest architecture that meets the needs, as a component list and a text diagram (client, API, services, database, queues, storage, auth).
2. Tech stack choices with one-line reasons tied to my team and constraints, plus one alternative for each.
3. A first-draft data model: main entities, key fields and relationships.
4. How each main user flow moves through the components.
5. Trade-offs and risks: what this design does badly, and the point at which it would need to change.
6. What to build first: a 3-milestone plan.

Prefer boring, well-known technology. Do not add microservices, caches or queues unless the requirements justify them, and say why if you do.

## Suspense film scene prompt for AI video

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/suspense-film-scene-video/
Category: Video
Works with: Veo, Kling, Runway and Seedance
Published: 2026-11-21

Build tension in a short AI video scene using framing, slow camera moves, light and sound cues — for trailers, shorts and story teasers.

Prompt:

Create a [LENGTH, E.G. 10-SECOND] cinematic suspense scene, [ASPECT, E.G. 2.39:1 WIDESCREEN].

Setting: [SETTING, E.G. EMPTY FARMHOUSE KITCHEN AT NIGHT, RAIN ON THE WINDOWS]
Character: [CHARACTER DESCRIPTION AND WHAT THEY ARE DOING]
Light: [LIGHT, E.G. SINGLE FLICKERING CEILING BULB, DEEP SHADOWS, COLD BLUE MOONLIGHT FROM THE WINDOW]

Beat 1 (0–4s): wide static shot, the character stops and listens; nothing else moves.
Beat 2 (4–8s): very slow push-in towards [FOCUS POINT, E.G. THE HALF-OPEN DOOR]; the light flickers once.
Beat 3 (8–10s): [REVEAL OR CLIFFHANGER, E.G. A SHADOW PASSES BEHIND THE DOOR GAP], hold on the character's face.

Sound: [SOUND, E.G. RAIN, LOW HUM, A FLOORBOARD CREAK AT 7 SECONDS, THEN SILENCE]
Style: muted colour, high contrast, film grain, realistic, no gore, no text.
Avoid: fast movement, jump cuts, extra characters, distorted faces.

Prompt:

Type of change: [REDESIGN, NEW CMS, DOMAIN CHANGE, URL STRUCTURE CHANGE, HTTPS, MERGING SITES]

New site or platform: [NEW SITE]
Pages that bring most traffic or revenue: [KEY PAGES]

## 13-week cash flow forecast for a small business

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/13-week-cash-flow-forecast/
Category: Finance
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Prompt:

Expected incoming payments (customer, amount, expected date): [RECEIPTS]
Typical payment delays from customers: [E.G. 15 DAYS LATE ON AVERAGE]
Regular costs (rent, payroll, software, loan payments, with dates): [FIXED COSTS]
Variable or one-off costs: [OTHER COSTS AND DATES]
Taxes due: [TAX PAYMENTS AND DATES]

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/break-even-analysis/
Category: Finance
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Prompt:

You are a small business finance tutor. Do a break-even analysis with my numbers.

Product or business: [WHAT YOU SELL]
Selling price per unit: [PRICE]
Variable cost per unit (materials, packaging, fees, shipping): [COSTS PER UNIT]
Fixed costs per month (rent, salaries, software, insurance): [FIXED COSTS]
Expected sales per month: [UNITS]
Currency: [CURRENCY]

Calculate and explain:
1. Contribution margin per unit and contribution margin ratio, with formulas.
2. Break-even point in units and in revenue per month.
3. Margin of safety based on my expected sales.

6. Units needed to reach a target monthly profit of [TARGET PROFIT].
7. Three practical ways to lower the break-even point.

Show every calculation step and present results in a table I can copy into a spreadsheet. Flag any cost I may have missed (e.g. payment fees, returns).

## Scenario planning for best, base and worst cases

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/business-scenario-planning/
Category: Strategy
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Explore how your business performs in three realistic futures, with early warning signs and actions to prepare for each scenario.

Prompt:

Business: [WHAT YOU DO, MARKET, SIZE]
Planning horizon: [E.G. 12 MONTHS, 3 YEARS]
Current plan and key numbers: [REVENUE, COSTS, GROWTH TARGET]
Biggest uncertainties I see: [E.G. DEMAND, PRICES, REGULATION, A KEY CUSTOMER, TECHNOLOGY]
Resources and constraints: [CASH, TEAM, CONTRACTS]

## Clean messy data with clear step-by-step rules

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/clean-messy-data-rules/
Category: Data analysis
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Get a cleaning plan for a messy spreadsheet or CSV, covering duplicates, formats, missing values and typos, plus a script or formulas to apply it.

Prompt:

You are a data analyst. Help me clean this dataset.

What the data is and what I'll use it for: [DATA AND PURPOSE]
Column list with a short description of each: [COLUMNS]
A sample of 20–50 rows (including messy ones): [SAMPLE ROWS]
Tool I'll use: [EXCEL, GOOGLE SHEETS, PYTHON PANDAS, SQL]

Do this:
1. List every data quality problem you see in the sample, by column (duplicates, formats, missing values, typos, outliers, mixed units).
2. Propose a cleaning rule for each, and note any rule that needs my decision (e.g. drop or fill missing values).
3. Write the code or formulas for my tool to apply all rules, with comments.
4. Add checks to run after cleaning (row counts, unique values, ranges).
5. Suggest how to stop the same problems at the source (form validation, drop-down lists).

Never delete data without telling me which rule removes it and how many rows it affects in the sample.

About the author or company (real credentials, experience): [AUTHOR DETAILS]

## Prioritise your to-do list with the Eisenhower matrix

Category: Productivity
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Sort a long task list into do now, schedule, delegate and drop, then get a realistic plan for today based on your time.

My main goals this month: [GOALS]
Hours available today: [HOURS]
People I can delegate to: [NAMES OR ROLES, OR "NONE"]
Energy pattern: [E.G. FOCUSED IN THE MORNING]

Do this:
1. Rewrite any vague task into a clear next action (verb + object).
2. Sort tasks into four groups: Do now (urgent and important), Schedule (important, not urgent), Delegate (urgent, not important), Drop or postpone (neither). Give a one-line reason for each.
3. Flag tasks that are really projects and need breaking down.
4. Build a plan for today that fits my hours, with the hardest important task in my best energy slot and buffer time.

2. Show a table: sender, subject, category, reason, deadline if mentioned.
3. For each email needing a reply, draft a response under 100 words in my tone. Where I need to make a decision or provide information, add a {DECIDE} or {FILL IN} marker instead of guessing.
4. List any commitments or deadlines found in the emails so I can add them to my calendar.
5. Suggest 2–3 filters or templates that would prevent this backlog next time.

Be brief and polite. Don't promise anything on my behalf.

## Email subject lines worth A/B testing

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/email-subject-line-tests/
Category: Marketing
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Get 15 email subject lines in five different styles, with preview text and a simple plan for testing which one gets more opens.

Prompt:

You are an email marketer. Write subject lines for this email.

What the email is about: [EMAIL TOPIC OR OFFER]
Audience: [WHO RECEIVES IT]
Brand tone: [E.G. FRIENDLY, EXPERT, PLAYFUL]
Goal of the email: [OPEN AND CLICK, BUY, REGISTER, READ]
Words or claims to avoid: [ANYTHING OFF-LIMITS]

Write 15 subject lines, 3 in each style:
1. Curiosity (opens a question without being vague clickbait)
2. Direct benefit (says plainly what the reader gets)
3. Urgency or timing (only if the email really has a deadline; otherwise use relevance to now)
4. Personal / conversational (sounds like a note from a person)
5. Specific number or detail

Rules: under 50 characters where possible, no ALL CAPS, no more than one emoji in the whole set, no misleading promises.
For each line add preview text (40–90 characters) that adds new information instead of repeating the subject.
Finish with your top 2 picks for an A/B test and what each one tests.

## Fact-check a draft before publishing

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/fact-check-draft-before-publishing/
Category: Research
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

List every checkable claim in your article or report, flag the risky ones and get guidance on what source would confirm each.

Prompt:

You are a meticulous fact-checker. Review my draft before publication.

Draft: [DRAFT]
Where it will be published and for whom: [PUBLICATION AND AUDIENCE]
Sources I used (links or notes): [SOURCES OR "NONE"]

Do this:
1. Extract every checkable claim: numbers, dates, names, quotes, cause-and-effect statements, comparisons, "first/only/biggest" claims.
2. For each, give a table row: the claim (quoted), type, risk level (high/medium/low) and why, whether one of my sources seems to support it, and what kind of source would confirm it.

4. Flag claims about real people or companies that could be unfair or defamatory if wrong.
5. List claims that would be safer with hedging (e.g. "according to…").

Don't mark anything as verified yourself — I'll confirm each one against original sources.

## Image alt text in bulk for SEO and accessibility

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/image-alt-text-bulk/

Published: 2026-11-20

Prompt:

Page topic and purpose: [PAGE TOPIC]
Main keyword (use only where it naturally fits): [KEYWORD]
Images — for each: file name, what it shows, and its role on the page (product, decorative, chart, step in a tutorial): [IMAGE LIST]

Rules:
1. Describe what matters in the image for this page, in under 125 characters.
2. Don't start with "image of" or "picture of".

## Jobs-to-be-done interview script

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/jobs-to-be-done-interview/
Category: Research
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Get an interview guide that uncovers why customers really switched to your product, plus a template to analyse their answers.

Prompt:

You are a product researcher experienced in jobs-to-be-done interviews. Create an interview guide.

Product: [WHAT IT IS]
Who to interview: [RECENT CUSTOMERS WHO BOUGHT IN THE LAST X MONTHS / CUSTOMERS WHO LEFT]
What we want to learn: [E.G. WHY PEOPLE SWITCH FROM SPREADSHEETS]
Interview length: [MINUTES]

Create:
1. A short intro script that sets the person at ease and explains there are no wrong answers.
2. Questions in timeline order: first thought (when they first realised they needed something), passive looking, active looking, deciding, first use, and now. 3–5 open questions per stage.
3. Follow-up probes to dig deeper ("What happened right before that?", "What else did you try?").
4. Questions to uncover the four forces: push of the current situation, pull of the new solution, anxieties, and habits holding them back.
5. Things the interviewer should avoid (leading questions, pitching, asking about the future).
6. An analysis template: job statement ("When I…, I want to…, so I can…"), triggers, alternatives considered, forces, outcomes wanted.

## Literature review matrix from your sources

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/literature-review-matrix/
Category: Research
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Organise research papers into a comparison matrix of aims, methods, findings and gaps, then draft a synthesis paragraph by theme.

Prompt:

You are an academic research assistant. Help me build a literature review matrix.

Research question: [YOUR QUESTION]
Field and level: [E.G. PUBLIC HEALTH, MASTER'S THESIS]
Sources (paste abstracts or notes, each with author and year): [SOURCES]
Citation style: [APA / HARVARD / MLA / OTHER]

Do this:
1. Create a table with columns: source (author, year), aim, method and sample, key findings, limitations, relevance to my question.
2. Group the sources into 3–5 themes and list which sources belong to each.
3. Identify where sources agree, where they disagree and possible reasons (method, sample, context).
4. List research gaps that my study could address.
5. Draft one synthesis paragraph per theme (120–180 words), comparing sources rather than summarising one by one, with in-text citations.

Rules: use only the sources I provided. Never add papers, authors or findings that are not in my input. If an abstract lacks a detail (e.g. sample size), write "not stated".

## Market size estimate with TAM, SAM and SOM

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/market-size-estimate/
Category: Research
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Estimate your total, serviceable and obtainable market bottom-up, with every assumption shown so you can check and adjust it.

Prompt:

You are a market research analyst. Estimate the market size for my business using a bottom-up method.

Product and price: [WHAT YOU SELL AND AT WHAT PRICE]
Customer type: [WHO PAYS]
Geography: [COUNTRIES OR REGIONS]
Data I have (customer counts, industry figures, my sales): [DATA AND SOURCES]
Sales channels and capacity: [HOW YOU SELL AND HOW MANY CUSTOMERS YOU CAN SERVE]

Do this:
1. TAM: all potential buyers × annual revenue per buyer. Show the formula.
2. SAM: the part of TAM you can actually reach with your product, channels and geography. Explain each filter.
3. SOM: a realistic share in 3 years given your capacity and competition. Give low, base and high cases.
4. Put every assumption in a table with columns: assumption, value, source or reasoning, confidence (low/medium/high), how to verify.
5. Do not invent statistics. Where you need a number I didn't give, use a clearly labelled placeholder like {NUMBER OF X — find in national statistics} and show how the result changes.

End with the 3 assumptions that most affect the result.

## Monthly investor update email for founders

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/monthly-investor-update/
Category: Strategy
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Write a concise investor update with key metrics, wins, challenges and specific asks, so investors stay informed and can help.

Prompt:

You are a startup founder's chief of staff. Write this month's investor update from my notes.

Company and stage: [COMPANY, WHAT IT DOES, STAGE]
Month: [MONTH]
Key metrics this month and last month: [E.G. REVENUE, USERS, BURN, RUNWAY]
Wins: [WINS]
Challenges and what we're doing about them: [CHALLENGES]
Product and team updates: [UPDATES]
Specific asks (intros, hires, advice): [ASKS]

Format:
1. Subject line: "[Company] update — [Month]: [one-line headline]".
2. TL;DR in 3 bullets.
3. Metrics table: metric, this month, last month, change.
4. Wins (3–5 bullets).
5. Challenges (honest, with the plan).
6. Product and team.
7. Asks — numbered and specific (who, what, why).
8. Short thank-you.

Under 400 words. Use only my numbers; never round up or add metrics. Tone: direct and confident, no hype.

---

## Mutual action plan to close a B2B deal

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/mutual-action-plan-b2b/
Category: Sales
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Build a shared plan with your buyer listing every step, owner and date until signature, so complex B2B deals don't stall or slip.

Prompt:

You are an enterprise sales coach. Draft a mutual action plan for this deal.

Buyer company and what they want to achieve: [BUYER AND GOAL]
Our solution: [SOLUTION]
People involved on their side (names or roles) and their concerns: [STAKEHOLDERS]
Their target go-live date and why it matters: [DATE AND REASON]
Where the deal stands now: [CURRENT STAGE]
Their buying process, as far as I know (legal, security, procurement): [PROCESS]

Create:
1. A one-paragraph summary of the buyer's goal and success criteria, in their language.
2. A table working backwards from go-live: step, owner (their side / our side), due date, status.
3. Steps I'm likely missing for a deal like this (e.g. security review, budget approval).
4. 3 questions to ask the champion to confirm the plan.
5. A short email to send the plan to the buyer and ask for edits.

Keep the plan collaborative — it should read like a shared project plan, not a sales pitch.

## Neighbourhood guide for home buyers

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/neighborhood-guide-buyers/
Category: Real estate
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Create a helpful neighbourhood guide for buyers covering lifestyle, amenities, transport and things to check, from your local knowledge.

Prompt:

You are a real estate content writer. Write a neighbourhood guide for home buyers.

Neighbourhood and city: [AREA, CITY]
Who often buys here: [E.G. FIRST-TIME BUYERS, PEOPLE WORKING DOWNTOWN]
Local facts I can confirm (parks, cafes, shops, transport links, commute times, schools by name, events): [FACTS]
Typical homes: [HOUSE TYPES, AGE, PRICE RANGE IF KNOWN]
My business and contact: [AGENT OR AGENCY]

Write:
1. A title and intro (80 words) on the area's character.
2. Sections: Getting around, Everyday shopping and food, Parks and outdoors, Schools and childcare (facts only, no rankings unless I provided a source), Homes you'll find here, Things to check before buying (e.g. parking, noise, flood maps — as questions to research).
3. "A Saturday in [area]" — a short, realistic description based on my facts.
4. A soft call to action to contact me.
5. An SEO title (under 60 characters) and meta description.

Rules: use only facts I gave; mark gaps {ADD LOCAL DETAIL}. Describe places and amenities, never the people who live there. Avoid words about neighbourhood "type" of residents, safety claims or anything that could steer buyers, to stay within fair housing rules.

## 30-60-90 day onboarding plan for a new hire

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/new-hire-onboarding-plan/
Category: HR
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Create a structured onboarding plan with first-week tasks, people to meet, training and clear 30, 60 and 90-day goals for any role.

Prompt:

You are an HR and people operations specialist. Create an onboarding plan for a new hire.

Role and seniority: [JOB TITLE AND LEVEL]
Team and manager: [TEAM, WHO THEY REPORT TO]
Work setup: [REMOTE / HYBRID / OFFICE]
Key tools and systems: [TOOLS]
What success in this role looks like after 6 months: [OUTCOMES]
Company specifics to include: [VALUES, POLICIES, RITUALS]

Create:
1. A pre-start checklist (accounts, equipment, welcome message, buddy assigned).
2. Day 1 and week 1, day by day: meetings, setup, reading, one small first task.
3. People to meet in the first 2 weeks, with the purpose of each meeting.
4. 30-day goals (learn), 60-day goals (contribute), 90-day goals (own) — 3–4 measurable goals each.
5. Check-in schedule with 3 questions the manager should ask at each check-in.
6. A short list of common onboarding mistakes for this type of role and how to avoid them.

Format as a clear plan the manager can copy into a document and share with the new hire.

## Weekly newsletter from a list of links

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/newsletter-from-links/
Category: Writing
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Turn a pile of saved links and notes into a readable newsletter with a short intro, grouped sections and your own take on each item.

Prompt:

You are the editor of my newsletter. Turn my links and notes into this week's issue.

Newsletter name and audience: [NAME AND WHO READS IT]
My tone: [E.G. DRY AND SMART, WARM, PRACTICAL]
Links with my notes (paste content or summaries, not just URLs): [LINKS AND NOTES]
Anything personal to mention this week: [OPTIONAL NEWS OR STORY]

Write:
1. Three subject line options.
2. An intro of 60–100 words that connects the main theme of the week.
3. 2–4 sections grouping the items by theme, each with a short heading.
4. For each item: a bold one-line title, 2–3 sentences on what it is and why it matters to my readers, and {MY TAKE} where I should add my opinion.
5. A short sign-off with one question that invites replies.

Rules: summarise only what is in my notes; if an item has no content, mark it {NEEDS SUMMARY} instead of guessing what the link says.

## Turn your strategy into clear quarterly OKRs

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/okrs-from-strategy/
Category: Strategy
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Convert goals into 3–4 objectives with measurable key results, owners and first initiatives, and catch weak OKRs before you commit.

Prompt:

You are an OKR coach. Help me write OKRs for next quarter.

Company or team: [WHO THE OKRS ARE FOR]
Strategy and priorities for this year: [STRATEGY]
Current numbers we can measure from: [BASELINE METRICS]
Last quarter's results and lessons: [WHAT HAPPENED]
Team size and capacity: [PEOPLE AND CONSTRAINTS]

Do this:
1. Propose 3–4 objectives: short, qualitative, inspiring, each linked to a strategy priority.
2. For each objective write 2–4 key results that are measurable outcomes with a baseline and a target (from → to). No tasks as key results.
3. List 2–3 initiatives (the work) per objective, separately from the key results.
4. Suggest an owner role for each key result.
5. Check every key result: Is it an outcome? Can we measure it weekly or monthly? Is it ambitious but possible? Flag weak ones and rewrite them.
6. Name what we are choosing NOT to focus on this quarter.

If a baseline is missing, write {BASELINE NEEDED} rather than inventing one.

## On-page SEO audit for a single page

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/on-page-seo-audit/
Category: SEO
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Check one page's title, headings, content, internal links, images and search intent match, and get a prioritised list of fixes.

Prompt:

You are an SEO consultant. Audit this page.

URL and target keyword: [URL AND KEYWORD]
Secondary keywords: [SECONDARY KEYWORDS]
What currently ranks for the keyword (titles or page types, if known): [TOP RESULTS]
Page HTML or content, including title tag, meta description and headings: [PAGE CONTENT]

Check and comment on:
1. Search intent match — does the page type and angle fit what searchers want?
2. Title tag and meta description — length, keyword, appeal. Suggest 3 alternatives.
3. Headings — one H1, logical H2/H3 structure, keyword use.
4. Content — coverage of subtopics, depth, freshness, readability, missing questions.
5. Internal links — in and out, anchor text; suggest 3–5 links.
6. Images — alt text, file names, size hints.
7. Structured data opportunities.
8. Calls to action and user experience issues visible in the content.

Finish with a table of fixes: issue, fix, impact (high/medium/low), effort (low/medium/high), sorted by impact.

## Open house follow-up emails for buyers

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/open-house-follow-up-email/
Category: Real estate
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Write personal follow-up emails for open house visitors based on their interest level, with property highlights and a clear next step.

Prompt:

You are a real estate agent. Write follow-up emails to open house visitors.

Property: [ADDRESS OR SHORT DESCRIPTION]
Key features and price: [FEATURES AND PRICE]
Notes about visitors (names, what they liked, concerns, buying stage): [VISITOR NOTES]
My name, agency and contact details: [MY DETAILS]
Next steps I can offer: [E.G. PRIVATE VIEWING, DISCLOSURE PACK, SIMILAR LISTINGS]

Write:
1. A "hot lead" email for serious buyers — reference what they liked, answer their concern, offer a private viewing with two time options.
2. A "warm lead" email — thank them, share 2–3 highlights and one useful document, invite questions.
3. A "just looking" email — friendly thanks and an offer to send similar listings.
4. A short text message version of each (under 300 characters).
5. A second follow-up for non-responders, 4 days later.

Personal, helpful tone, under 120 words per email. Don't invent property facts or pressure buyers with fake competing offers.

## Painterly pet portrait from a photo

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/painterly-pet-portrait/
Category: Image
Works with: GPT Image, Midjourney and Flux
Published: 2026-11-20

Turn a photo of your dog or cat into a classic oil-painting style portrait that keeps their real markings, for gifts or prints.

Prompt:

Portrait of my [DOG / CAT], a [BREED OR MIX] with [EXACT COAT COLOURS AND MARKINGS, E.G. WHITE CHEST, BROWN PATCH OVER LEFT EYE, ONE FLOPPY EAR], based on the uploaded reference photo. Keep the face, markings and expression true to the photo.
Style: classic oil painting with visible soft brushstrokes, rich colours, gentle chiaroscuro lighting.
Pose: [SITTING UPRIGHT / LYING ON A VELVET CUSHION / HEAD AND SHOULDERS].
Setting: [DARK WARM BACKGROUND / COUNTRY GARDEN / COSY LIBRARY].
Optional accessory: [E.G. A SMALL BOW TIE, A FLOWER CROWN, NONE].
Framing: centred, plenty of space around for printing and framing.
Aspect ratio [4:5].

## Partnership proposal email to another business

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/partnership-proposal-email/
Category: Strategy
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Write a short partnership pitch to a complementary business that shows the mutual benefit, suggests a simple first project and asks for a call.

Prompt:

You are a business development manager. Write a partnership proposal email.

My business and audience: [MY BUSINESS AND AUDIENCE]
Their business and audience: [THEIR BUSINESS AND AUDIENCE]
Why our audiences overlap or complement each other: [OVERLAP]
Partnership idea: [E.G. JOINT WEBINAR, REFERRAL DEAL, PRODUCT BUNDLE]
What I can offer them: [WHAT I BRING]
Contact name and role: [CONTACT]

Write:
1. 3 subject line options.
2. An email under 150 words: a personal, specific opening about their business; the shared audience; the idea and what's in it for them; a small first step (e.g. one co-hosted session); a simple ask for a 20-minute call.
3. A follow-up email for 5 days later, under 70 words.
4. A one-page outline of the partnership I can attach if they're interested: goals, roles, timeline, how we'll measure it.

Friendly and direct. No flattery, no inflated numbers.

## Pinterest pin titles and descriptions that get saves

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/pinterest-pin-titles-descriptions/
Category: Marketing
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Write keyword-rich Pinterest pin titles, descriptions and text overlays for a blog post or product, plus board names that help pins get found.

Prompt:

You are a Pinterest marketing specialist. Create pins for this link.

Link and what it offers: [URL AND CONTENT SUMMARY]
Audience: [AUDIENCE]
Main keyword and related search phrases: [KEYWORDS]
Brand voice: [VOICE]

Create 5 pin variations, each with a different angle (e.g. how-to, list, problem/solution, inspiration, checklist). For each:
1. Pin title (under 100 characters) with the keyword near the start.
2. Description (200–400 characters) written naturally for searchers, ending with a reason to click.
3. Text overlay for the image (max 8 words).
4. Image idea (what the visual should show).

Then:
5. 3 board names that people would search for, with a one-line board description each.
6. Alt text for each pin image.

No hashtag stuffing; at most 2–3 relevant hashtags per description.

## Plan a feature before the AI writes code

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/plan-feature-before-coding/
Category: Coding
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Make the AI ask questions, map affected files and agree on a design before coding, which cuts hallucinated APIs and wasted rewrites.

Prompt:

You are a senior software engineer. Before writing any code, help me plan this feature.

Feature request: [WHAT THE FEATURE SHOULD DO, FROM THE USER'S POINT OF VIEW]
Tech stack and versions: [LANGUAGES, FRAMEWORKS, DATABASE]
Relevant code (files, models, routes): [PASTE OR DESCRIBE]
Constraints: [PERFORMANCE, SECURITY, DEADLINES, CONVENTIONS]

Step 1 — Ask me up to 7 clarifying questions about requirements and edge cases. Wait for my answers.
Step 2 — After my answers, write:
  a) A short spec: user stories and acceptance criteria.
  b) Assumptions you're making, each one I can confirm or reject.
  c) The files and functions that need to change or be created, and why.
  d) Data model or API changes.
  e) Risks and edge cases (errors, permissions, empty states, concurrency).
  f) A step-by-step implementation plan in small commits, with tests for each.
Step 3 — Only after I approve the plan, implement step 1.

Rules: use only functions and libraries that exist in the code I shared or in the official docs of my stack versions. If you're not sure an API exists, say so instead of guessing.

## Podcast guest pitch email that hosts accept

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/podcast-guest-pitch-email/
Category: Marketing
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Write a short, personalised pitch to appear as a guest on a podcast, with episode ideas that suit the show and proof you'll be a good guest.

Prompt:

You are a PR specialist. Write a podcast guest pitch.

Podcast name, host and audience: [PODCAST, HOST, AUDIENCE]
An episode I listened to and what I liked about it: [EPISODE AND DETAIL]
Who I am and my expertise: [MY BACKGROUND]
Topics I can speak about with real experience: [TOPICS]
Proof I'm a good guest (past interviews, talks, audience): [PROOF OR "NONE"]

Write:
1. 3 subject line options.
2. A pitch under 150 words: a genuine reference to the show, who I am in one line, 3 episode ideas with a hook title and what listeners will learn, why now, and a simple ask.
3. A short follow-up email for 7 days later.
4. A one-paragraph guest bio and 5 questions the host could ask me.

Friendly and specific. No exaggerated claims about my audience or results.

## Press release for news journalists will read

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/press-release-writer/
Category: Writing
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Write a press release with a news-led headline, the key facts up top, a usable quote and a boilerplate, plus a short pitch email.

Prompt:

You are a PR writer. Write a press release.

Company: [NAME, WHAT IT DOES, LOCATION]
The news: [LAUNCH, PARTNERSHIP, FUNDING, EVENT, HIRE]
Why it matters and to whom: [IMPACT]
Key facts (dates, numbers, availability, price): [FACTS]
Approved quote(s) from a named spokesperson: [QUOTE OR ROUGH POINTS FOR A QUOTE]
Target media: [E.G. LOCAL NEWS, TRADE PRESS FOR LOGISTICS]
Contact details: [MEDIA CONTACT]

Write:
1. Headline (under 12 words) stating the news, and a one-sentence subheadline.
2. Dateline and first paragraph answering who, what, when, where and why.
3. Second paragraph with context and details.
4. A quote that adds a view or insight, not just "we're excited". If I gave rough points, write a draft and mark it {NEEDS SPOKESPERSON APPROVAL}.
5. Availability or next steps.
6. Boilerplate "About [Company]" (50–80 words).
7. Media contact.
8. A pitch email to a journalist (under 120 words) with a news angle for their audience.

Rules: no hype words, no unverifiable superlatives, no invented numbers.

## Announce a price increase without losing customers

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/price-increase-announcement/
Category: Strategy
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Write a clear, honest price increase email that explains the reason, shows the value and gives customers time and options.

Prompt:

You are a customer communications specialist. Write a price increase announcement.

Business and product: [WHAT YOU SELL]
Current price and new price: [OLD → NEW, PER PLAN IF SEVERAL]
Date the new price starts: [DATE]
Honest reason for the increase: [E.G. HIGHER COSTS, NEW FEATURES, MORE SUPPORT]
What customers got recently or will get: [IMPROVEMENTS]
Options we can offer: [E.G. LOCK IN ANNUAL PLAN AT OLD PRICE, DOWNGRADE, GRANDFATHERING]
Tone: [WARM / DIRECT / FORMAL]

Write:
1. Three subject lines that are clear, not clever.
2. An email of 150–220 words: the change and date in the first two sentences, the reason in plain words, the value, the options, and how to get help.
3. A 5-question FAQ for the help page.
4. A reply template for a customer who says the new price is too high.

Rules: no guilt, no hype, no "exciting news". Do not invent features or numbers I didn't give.

## Privacy policy draft for a small website

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/privacy-policy-draft-website/
Category: Legal
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Draft a plain-language privacy policy for a small website or app based on the data you actually collect, the tools you use and where users live.

Prompt:

You are helping me draft a privacy policy for review by a qualified professional. This is not legal advice.

Website or app and what it does: [SITE AND PURPOSE]
Business name, location and contact email: [BUSINESS DETAILS]
Where users are located: [E.G. EU, UK, US, WORLDWIDE]
Personal data collected and how (forms, accounts, cookies, payments): [DATA COLLECTED]
Why each type is used: [PURPOSES]
Third-party tools (analytics, email, payments, ads, hosting): [TOOLS]
How long data is kept: [RETENTION]

Draft sections: who we are; what data we collect; how and why we use it (with legal basis where relevant); cookies and similar tools; who we share data with; international transfers; how long we keep it; user rights and how to use them; children; security; changes to this policy; contact.

Plain language, short paragraphs. Only describe the practices I listed. Mark anything that depends on specific laws or that I haven't told you with {CHECK}.

## Product 360 turntable video prompt

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/product-360-turntable-video/
Category: Video
Works with: Veo, Kling, Runway and Seedance
Published: 2026-11-20

Generate a smooth 360-degree turntable video of your product on a clean background, showing every side for product pages and ads.

Prompt:

Smooth 360-degree turntable video of [PRODUCT], based on the attached reference image.
The product sits on a [SURFACE, E.G. MATTE WHITE ROUND PEDESTAL] and rotates slowly and evenly clockwise one full turn.
Camera: fixed, eye level, slightly above the product, no zoom, no camera movement.
Background: seamless [BACKGROUND COLOUR] studio backdrop.
Lighting: soft three-point studio lighting, gentle reflections, soft shadow under the product.
The product's shape, colours, logo and details must stay accurate and identical from every angle. Duration 8 seconds, seamless loop, no text, no hands. Aspect ratio [1:1, 4:5 OR 16:9].

## Product unboxing video clip prompt

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/product-unboxing-video/

Close-up top-down video of hands unboxing [PRODUCT] from a [PACKAGING DESCRIPTION, E.G. MATTE BLACK BOX WITH GOLD LOGO] on a [SURFACE, E.G. LIGHT OAK TABLE]. Soft natural window light from the left, shallow depth of field.
Shot 1 (0–3s): hands slowly lift the lid; tissue paper inside.

## Project risk register with owners and actions

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/project-risk-register/
Category: Strategy
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Identify the risks in a project, score their likelihood and impact, and assign owners, early warning signs and actions to reduce each one.

Prompt:

You are a project manager. Build a risk register for my project.

Project goal and scope: [PROJECT]
Timeline and key milestones: [TIMELINE]
Team and key stakeholders: [TEAM]
Budget: [BUDGET]
Dependencies (vendors, other teams, approvals, technology): [DEPENDENCIES]
Concerns I already have: [CONCERNS]

Create:
1. 12–15 risks across categories: scope, schedule, budget, people, technical, external, stakeholder.
2. A table: ID, risk (written as "If… then…"), category, likelihood 1–5, impact 1–5, score, early warning sign, response (avoid, reduce, transfer, accept), specific action, owner role, review date.
3. Sort by score and highlight the top 5.
4. Assumptions the plan depends on that should be checked now.
5. A short agenda for a 30-minute risk review meeting.

Make risks specific to my project, not generic.

## Quiz questions with answer explanations

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/quiz-with-explanations/
Category: Education
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Create a multiple-choice quiz with realistic wrong answers and short explanations that teach, at the difficulty level you choose.

Prompt:

You are an experienced teacher and assessment designer. Create a quiz.

Topic or material (paste text if possible): [TOPIC OR NOTES]
Learners and level: [E.G. GRADE 8, FIRST-YEAR NURSING STUDENTS, NEW EMPLOYEES]
Number of questions: [NUMBER]
Difficulty mix: [E.G. 40% RECALL, 40% UNDERSTANDING, 20% APPLICATION]

For each question:
1. A clear question stem (no "all of the above" or trick wording).
2. Four options, one correct. Wrong options must be based on common mistakes or misconceptions.
3. The correct answer.
4. A 1–2 sentence explanation of why it is correct and why the most tempting wrong answer is wrong.
5. The skill it tests (recall, understanding, application).

Rules: base every question only on the material provided; if it is thin, tell me what is missing instead of inventing facts. Vary the position of the correct answer.
End with an answer key table.

## README file for your code project

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/readme-for-code-project/
Category: Coding
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Write a clear README with setup steps, usage examples, configuration and contributing notes, based on your project's real files.

Prompt:

You are a technical writer for developers. Write a README.md for my project.

Project name and one-line purpose: [NAME AND PURPOSE]
Who it's for: [AUDIENCE]
Language, framework and key dependencies: [STACK]
File tree (top two levels): [FILE TREE]
Package file / build config (e.g. package.json, pyproject.toml): [CONFIG FILE CONTENT]
How I run it locally and any environment variables: [COMMANDS AND ENV VARS]
License: [LICENSE]

Include these sections: title and short description, features, requirements, installation, quick start with a working example, configuration (table of env vars with defaults), project structure, running tests, contributing, license.

Use only commands and file names that appear in my input. If something needed is missing (e.g. how to run tests), add a TODO note instead of inventing it. Use fenced code blocks with language tags.

## Real estate drone-style video tour prompt

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/real-estate-drone-video/
Category: Video
Works with: Veo, Kling, Runway and Seedance
Published: 2026-11-20

Create a smooth aerial-style property video that reveals the home, garden and surroundings for listings and social media.

Prompt:

Aerial drone-style shot of [PROPERTY TYPE, E.G. TWO-STOREY BRICK HOUSE WITH A GREY ROOF] surrounded by [GARDEN, TREES, STREET, POOL — WHAT IS REALLY THERE].
Time of day: [GOLDEN HOUR / CLEAR MIDDAY / BLUE HOUR WITH WARM WINDOW LIGHTS].
Camera: slow, steady drone move — [RISING UP AND TILTING DOWN TO REVEAL THE PROPERTY / SLOW ORBIT AROUND THE HOUSE / GLIDING FORWARD TOWARDS THE FRONT DOOR], [6–8] seconds, no cuts.
Style: realistic real estate cinematography, natural colours, sharp details, stable horizon.
Keep the building's shape, windows, roof and layout exactly as in the reference image.
Avoid: adding rooms, extra floors, pools or landscaping that are not in the reference; warping walls; people or cars appearing suddenly; text.

## Refactor legacy code without breaking it

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/refactor-legacy-code/
Category: Coding
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Get a step-by-step refactoring plan for messy code, with safety tests first and small changes you can review and ship one at a time.

Prompt:

You are a senior engineer who specialises in legacy code. Help me refactor this code safely.

Language and framework: [LANGUAGE / FRAMEWORK AND VERSION]
What the code does: [SHORT DESCRIPTION]
Main problems I see: [E.G. LONG FUNCTION, DUPLICATION, HARD TO TEST]
Constraints: [PUBLIC API MUST NOT CHANGE, NO NEW DEPENDENCIES, ETC.]
Code:
[PASTE CODE]

Work in this order:
1. Explain what the code currently does, including edge cases and odd behaviour. Flag anything that looks like a bug but don't fix it yet — list it separately.
2. Write characterisation tests that capture the current behaviour, including the odd parts.
3. Propose a sequence of 4–8 small refactoring steps (extract function, rename, remove duplication, etc.). Each step must keep behaviour identical.
4. Show the code after each step, with a one-line reason.
5. Finish with the final version and a list of the possible bugs from step 1 for me to decide on.

Do not change behaviour, invent APIs or add libraries. If something is unclear, ask instead of assuming.

## Design a referral program people actually use

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/referral-program-design/
Category: Marketing
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Plan a customer referral program with the right reward, timing, sharing message and tracking, tailored to your business and margins.

Prompt:

You are a growth marketer. Design a referral program for my business.

Business and product: [WHAT YOU SELL]
Average order or customer value: [VALUE]
Gross margin or what I can afford per new customer: [BUDGET]
When customers are happiest: [E.G. AFTER FIRST RESULT, AFTER DELIVERY]
Tools I use: [STORE PLATFORM, EMAIL TOOL, CRM]

Design:
1. Reward options: two-sided vs. one-sided, discount vs. credit vs. gift vs. donation. Recommend one and show the cost per acquired customer.
2. Trigger moments: when and where to ask (email, in-app, receipt, packaging).
3. The share message: 3 short versions a customer can send by text, email or social, written in a natural voice.
4. Landing page outline for referred friends.
5. Rules: eligibility, limits and fraud prevention, in plain language.
6. Tracking: what to measure weekly.
7. A 30-day launch plan with tasks.

Keep it simple enough for a small team to run.

## Regex pattern from examples you provide

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/regex-from-examples/
Category: Coding
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Get a regular expression that matches your examples and rejects your counter-examples, with an explanation and test cases for your language.

Prompt:

You are a regex expert. Write a regular expression for me.

Language or tool where it will run: [E.G. JAVASCRIPT, PYTHON, POSTGRESQL, VS CODE SEARCH]
What I want to match or extract, in plain words: [GOAL]
Strings that SHOULD match (and what to capture): [MATCH EXAMPLES]
Strings that should NOT match: [NON-MATCH EXAMPLES]

Give me:
1. The regex, with the flags needed.
2. A part-by-part explanation.
3. A table testing it against every example I gave: string, expected, actual result, captured groups.
4. 5 edge cases I didn't think of and how the pattern handles them.
5. A code snippet in my language that uses it.
6. Warnings about performance (e.g. catastrophic backtracking) or cases where a parser would be better than regex.

Use syntax supported by my language only.

## Repurpose one podcast episode into a week of content

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/repurpose-podcast-episode/
Category: Marketing
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Turn a podcast or video transcript into show notes, social posts, short clip ideas, a newsletter section and quote graphics.

Prompt:

You are a content strategist. Repurpose this episode into multiple pieces of content.

Show name and audience: [SHOW AND LISTENERS]
Episode title and guest (if any): [TITLE, GUEST]
Platforms I use: [E.G. LINKEDIN, INSTAGRAM, X, NEWSLETTER, YOUTUBE SHORTS]
Transcript (with timestamps if possible): [TRANSCRIPT]

Create:
1. Show notes: 2-sentence summary, 5 key takeaways, timestamps for main sections.
2. 5 short clip ideas: timestamp range, why it works, a hook line for the caption.
3. 3 LinkedIn posts, each built on a different idea from the episode.
4. 5 short posts for X or Threads.
5. 3 quote graphics: exact quotes from the transcript (word for word), with speaker name.
6. A newsletter section (150 words) that makes people want to listen.
7. A 7-day posting schedule using these pieces.

Rules: quotes must be copied exactly from the transcript. Don't add claims the speakers didn't make.

## Pull key findings from a research paper

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/research-paper-key-findings/
Category: Research
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Turn a dense academic paper into a clear summary of the question, method, findings, limitations and what it means for your own work.

Prompt:

You are a careful research assistant. Summarise this paper for me.

My background and why I'm reading it: [YOUR FIELD AND PURPOSE]
Paper text (or abstract, methods, results and discussion): [PAPER TEXT]

Give me:
1. The research question in one sentence.
2. Method: design, sample size, population, duration, key measures.
3. Main findings, each with the exact numbers reported (effect sizes, confidence intervals, p-values) and the page or section where they appear.
4. Limitations — both those the authors state and any obvious ones they don't (e.g. small sample, no control group, self-reported data).
5. How strong the evidence is on a scale of weak / moderate / strong, with one sentence of reasoning.
6. What this means for my purpose, in 3 bullets.
7. 3 terms I may not know, explained simply.

Only use information from the text. If something is not reported, say "not reported" rather than guessing.

## Rewrite any text for a chosen reading level

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/rewrite-for-reading-level/
Category: Writing
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Make complex text easier to read for a specific audience and reading level while keeping every important fact, number and warning.

Prompt:

You are a plain-language editor. Rewrite this text for a new audience.

Original text: [TEXT]
Who will read it: [AUDIENCE, E.G. CUSTOMERS WITH NO TECHNICAL BACKGROUND]
Target reading level: [E.G. AGE 12 / GRADE 7]
Where it will be published: [CHANNEL]

Rules:
1. Short sentences (average under 15 words) and common words.
2. Explain or replace jargon; if a technical term must stay, define it in brackets the first time.
3. Use active voice and "you" where it fits.
4. Keep every fact, number, date, condition and warning from the original.
5. Use headings or bullet points if they make it easier to scan.

Then give me:
- A checklist of all key facts from the original and confirmation each appears in the rewrite.
- Any sentence where simplifying risks changing the meaning, so I can review it.
