## Spot risky clauses in a lease agreement

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/risky-clauses-lease-agreement/
Category: Legal
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Review a residential or commercial lease for unusual or one-sided clauses, hidden costs and missing protections before you sign it.

Prompt:

You are helping me understand a lease before I sign. You are not giving legal advice.

Lease type: [RESIDENTIAL OR COMMERCIAL]
Country / state where the property is: [LOCATION]
I am the: [TENANT OR LANDLORD]
What matters most to me: [PRIORITIES, E.G. FLEXIBILITY TO LEAVE EARLY, LOW EXTRA COSTS]
Lease text: [LEASE TEXT]

Do this:
1. Summarise the key terms in a table: rent, deposit, term, renewal, notice periods, rent increases, repairs, utilities, pets, subletting, early termination.
2. List clauses that seem unusual, one-sided or unclear. For each: quote the clause, explain it simply, why it could be a problem for me, and a fairer alternative wording to propose.
3. List important protections that seem to be missing.
4. List all costs I could be charged beyond rent.
5. Give me 5 questions to ask before signing.

Quote the lease exactly when referring to it. Note that local laws may override some clauses, and suggest I confirm anything important with a local lawyer or tenant advice service.

## SaaS trial onboarding emails that drive activation

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/saas-trial-onboarding-emails/
Category: Marketing
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Write a trial onboarding email sequence that guides new users to their first success, nudges inactive ones and invites them to upgrade.

Prompt:

You are a SaaS lifecycle marketer. Write a trial onboarding email sequence.

Product and what it helps users do: [PRODUCT]
Trial length: [DAYS]
Key activation action (the moment users get value): [ACTIVATION ACTION]
2–3 setup steps needed before that: [SETUP STEPS]
Paid plans and price: [PLANS]
Tone: [TONE]

Write 6 emails:
1. Day 0 — welcome and the single first step.
2. Day 1 — how to reach the activation action (sent only if not done yet).
3. Day 3 — a use case or tip that shows more value.
4. Day 5 — help offer for stuck users (reply, docs, short call).
5. Two days before trial ends — what they'll lose and plan options.
6. Last day — simple upgrade reminder and an option to extend or give feedback.

For each: trigger condition, subject line, preview text, body under 120 words, one button.
Add a list of 3 behaviour-based emails to send when users complete key actions.

## Salary negotiation script for a job offer

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/salary-negotiation-script/
Category: Careers
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Prepare what to say when negotiating a job offer — your counter, reasons, answers to pushback and a polite email version.

Prompt:

You are a career coach who helps people negotiate offers. Prepare my salary negotiation.

Role and company: [JOB TITLE AT COMPANY TYPE]
Offer received: [BASE SALARY, BONUS, EQUITY, BENEFITS, START DATE]
Market range I found and where: [RANGE AND SOURCES]
My strongest reasons (skills, results, competing offers if real): [REASONS]
What matters most besides base pay: [E.G. REMOTE DAYS, TITLE, TRAINING BUDGET, START DATE]
My walk-away point: [MINIMUM]

Create:
1. A recommended counter-offer with a short reason for the number.
2. A call script: thank them, express interest, make the ask, then stop talking. Keep it natural.
3. Answers to 5 likely responses: "That's our max", "Budget is fixed", "What are you earning now?", "We need an answer today", "We can revisit in 6 months".
4. Non-salary items to ask for if base pay can't move, in priority order.
5. A polite negotiation email version (under 170 words).
6. How to accept gracefully once agreed, and what to get in writing.

Keep it confident and friendly, never aggressive. Don't invent offers I don't have.

## Sales battlecard against a competitor

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/sales-battlecard-competitor/
Category: Sales
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Build a one-page battlecard with where you win and lose against a competitor, landmine questions, objection replies and proof points.

Prompt:

You are a sales enablement manager. Build a battlecard.

Our product: [OUR PRODUCT]
Competitor: [COMPETITOR]
What we know about them (pricing, features, positioning, common complaints from public reviews or lost deals): [COMPETITOR FACTS]
Deals we won and lost against them, and why: [WIN AND LOSS NOTES]
Our ideal customer: [ICP]

Create a one-page battlecard:
1. Their pitch in one sentence, and ours.
2. Where we win (3–5 points) and where they win (be honest, 2–4 points).
3. Customer types for whom we are the better fit, and for whom they are.
4. 5 discovery questions that highlight our strengths without naming the competitor.
5. Replies to 4 common objections when they're in the deal.
6. Proof points we can use (only those I gave).
7. Things reps should never say about this competitor.

Only use the facts I provided. Mark anything that needs verification.

## Sales pitch deck outline that tells a story

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/sales-deck-outline/
Category: Sales
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Build a 10–12 slide sales deck outline that starts with the buyer's problem, proves value and ends with a clear next step.

Prompt:

You are a B2B sales coach. Outline a sales pitch deck.

What we sell: [PRODUCT OR SERVICE]
Target buyer (role and company type): [BUYER]
Their main problem: [PROBLEM]
What changes for them with us: [OUTCOME]
Proof we can honestly use (results, logos, demos): [PROOF]
Main competitors or the status quo: [ALTERNATIVES]
Meeting length: [MINUTES]

Create 10–12 slides in this order:
1. The shift in their world that makes the problem urgent
2. The cost of the problem today
3. What good looks like (the outcome)
4–6. How we deliver it (max three capabilities, each tied to an outcome)
7. Proof
8. Why us vs. the alternatives (fair, no attacks)
9. How it works / implementation steps
10. Pricing or investment framing
11. Next step with a date

For each slide give: a headline written as a statement (not a label), 2–3 bullet points, a visual idea and 2 sentences of speaker notes. Only use proof from my input.

## Sales demo script built around buyer problems

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/sales-demo-script/
Category: Sales
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Plan a product demo that starts with the buyer's problems, shows only the features that solve them and ends with a clear next step.

Prompt:

You are a sales engineer. Plan a product demo.

Product: [PRODUCT]
Buyer company and attendees (roles): [BUYER AND ATTENDEES]
Problems they shared in discovery: [PROBLEMS]
Their current tool or process: [CURRENT SOLUTION]
Demo length: [MINUTES]
Desired next step: [NEXT STEP]

Create:
1. An opening (2 minutes): agenda, recap of their problems in their words, and a check that nothing has changed.
2. For each problem: the "before" pain, the exact workflow to show (screens and clicks), the outcome to point out, and a question to ask afterwards.
3. Features NOT to show, because they don't relate to these problems.
4. Moments to stop and invite questions.
5. Likely objections from each attendee role and short answers.
6. A close: summary, confirm value, propose the next step with a date.
7. A timed run sheet.

Keep the demo conversational — the buyer should talk at least a third of the time.

## Sales voicemail scripts that get callbacks

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/sales-voicemail-scripts/
Category: Sales
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Write short voicemail scripts under 30 seconds for prospecting and follow-ups, each with a specific reason to call back and a matching email.

Prompt:

You are a sales coach. Write voicemail scripts.

What I sell: [PRODUCT]
Prospect role and company type: [PROSPECT]
Trigger or reason for reaching out (news, event, referral, common problem): [REASON]
My name, company and phone number: [MY DETAILS]

Write a sequence of 3 voicemails, each under 30 seconds when spoken (about 70 words):
1. First touch — who I am, the specific reason I'm calling, one question to think about, my number said twice.
2. Second touch — a new angle or useful idea.
3. Final touch — polite close of the loop.

For each voicemail also write:
- A matching email (under 80 words) to send right after, with a subject line that references the voicemail.
- The best time gap before the next touch.

Natural spoken language, no long company introductions, no false urgency. Mark pauses.

## Schema markup in JSON-LD for any page

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/schema-markup-json-ld/
Category: SEO
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Generate valid JSON-LD structured data for articles, products, FAQs, local businesses or events, using only the details on your page.

Prompt:

You are a technical SEO specialist. Write JSON-LD structured data for this page.

Page URL: [URL]
Page type (article, product, local business, FAQ, event, recipe, course, etc.): [PAGE TYPE]
Page content or key details (title, author, dates, prices, address, opening hours, FAQs…): [PAGE DETAILS]
Organisation name and logo URL: [ORGANISATION AND LOGO]

Do this:
1. Choose the most fitting schema.org type(s) and explain why in one sentence.
2. Write complete JSON-LD in a single <script type="application/ld+json"> block, using @graph if several types are needed.
3. Include only information that is visible on the page or that I provided — no invented ratings or reviews.
4. List required and recommended properties I haven't supplied.
5. Explain how to test it.

Output valid JSON with no comments inside the code.

## Search intent analysis for a keyword list

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/search-intent-keyword-list/
Category: SEO
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Classify a list of keywords by search intent and funnel stage, and get the best page type, content angle and priority for each one.

Prompt:

You are an SEO strategist. Analyse the search intent of these keywords.

My website and what it offers: [WEBSITE AND OFFER]
Keywords (with volume and difficulty if I have them): [KEYWORD LIST]
Pages I already have: [EXISTING PAGES OR "NONE"]

For each keyword give a table row:
- Intent: informational / commercial investigation / transactional / navigational
- Funnel stage: awareness / consideration / decision
- Best page type (guide, list, comparison, product, category, tool, landing page)
- Content angle in one line
- Whether an existing page should target it (name it) or a new page is needed
- Priority (high / medium / low), based on relevance to my offer and intent

Then:
1. Group keywords that one page could target together.
2. Flag keywords where intent is mixed or unclear and tell me what to check in the search results.
3. Suggest the first 5 pages to create.

Base volume or difficulty only on numbers I gave; don't invent them.

## Short story outline from a premise

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/short-story-outline-premise/
Category: Writing
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Develop a premise into a short story outline with a clear character goal, rising conflict, turning point and an ending that pays off.

Prompt:

You are a fiction editor. Help me outline a short story.

Premise: [PREMISE]
Genre and tone: [GENRE AND TONE]
Target length: [WORD COUNT]
Main character (what I know so far): [CHARACTER]
Themes or feelings I want readers left with: [THEMES]

Create:
1. Logline — one sentence with character, goal, obstacle and stakes.
2. Main character sheet: want, need, flaw, what they fear losing.
3. 3 possible endings in one line each, with the emotional effect of each. Recommend one.
4. A scene-by-scene outline (5–8 scenes) for the recommended ending: what happens, what changes, the conflict in the scene.
5. The turning point and how it is set up earlier.
6. 3 details or images that could recur and tie the story together.
7. 3 questions I should answer before drafting.

Give me structure and options only. Don't write the story's prose.

## Slow-motion sports action video prompt

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/slow-motion-sports-video/
Category: Video
Works with: Veo, Kling, Runway and Seedance
Published: 2026-11-20

Generate a dramatic slow-motion sports clip with a key moment, dynamic camera move and stadium or street lighting for promos and intros.

Prompt:

Cinematic slow-motion video, 120fps look, of [ATHLETE DESCRIPTION, E.G. A YOUNG BASKETBALL PLAYER IN A RED JERSEY] performing [ONE ACTION, E.G. A JUMP SHOT] at [LOCATION, E.G. AN OUTDOOR CITY COURT AT DUSK].
Camera: low angle, slow [CAMERA MOVE, E.G. ORBIT AROUND THE ATHLETE], ending on [FINAL FRAME, E.G. THE BALL LEAVING THE HANDS].
Details: sweat droplets, fabric rippling, dust or water particles in the air, realistic muscle movement.
Lighting: [LIGHTING, E.G. WARM BACKLIGHT FROM THE SETTING SUN WITH LENS FLARE].
Mood: focused, powerful, [BRAND MOOD]. Duration 6–8 seconds, no text, no slow-motion artefacts or extra limbs. Sound: muffled crowd, heartbeat, then a sharp [SOUND OF THE ACTION]. Aspect ratio [RATIO].

## Social media content pillars for your brand

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/social-media-content-pillars/
Category: Marketing
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Define 4–5 content pillars with post formats, example ideas and a weekly mix, so your social feed stays on-brand and never runs dry.

Prompt:

You are a social media strategist. Build content pillars for my brand.

Brand and what we sell: [BRAND AND OFFER]
Target audience and their main problems: [AUDIENCE AND PROBLEMS]
Platforms we use: [PLATFORMS]
Business goals for social media: [GOALS, E.G. LEADS, SALES, COMMUNITY]
Posts per week we can realistically make: [NUMBER]

Deliver:
1. 4–5 content pillars. For each: name, purpose (which goal it serves), what the audience gets from it, and what NOT to post under it.
2. For each pillar, 3 repeatable post formats (e.g. "myth vs fact carousel") suited to my platforms.
3. 5 specific post ideas per pillar, written as one-line hooks.
4. A weekly mix table: day, platform, pillar, format.
5. One metric per pillar to judge if it works.

Keep at least half of the posts useful even to people who never buy. Avoid generic ideas like "share a quote".

## Socratic tutor that guides you to the answer

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/socratic-tutor-guided-questions/
Category: Education
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Turn the AI into a patient tutor that asks guiding questions and gives hints instead of answers, so you actually learn to solve problems.

Prompt:

Act as a patient Socratic tutor for [SUBJECT] at [LEVEL, E.G. HIGH SCHOOL, FIRST-YEAR UNIVERSITY].

The problem or topic I'm working on: [PROBLEM OR TOPIC]
What I already understand or tried: [MY ATTEMPT]

Rules:
1. Never give me the final answer unless I type "show solution".
2. Start by asking what I think the first step is.
3. Ask one question at a time and wait for my reply.
4. If I'm wrong, don't just correct me — ask a question that helps me spot the mistake.
5. If I'm stuck twice in a row, give a small hint, then a bigger one if needed.
6. When I reach the answer, ask me to explain why it works in my own words.
7. Finish with one similar practice problem for me to try alone.

Keep messages short and encouraging. Use plain language and check my understanding of any new term.

## Write a clear SOP from a messy process

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/sop-from-messy-process/
Category: Productivity
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Turn rough notes, a voice transcript or a long chat about how a task is done into a step-by-step standard operating procedure with checks.

Prompt:

You are an operations manager. Turn my notes into a standard operating procedure.

Process name: [PROCESS]
Who will follow it: [ROLE AND EXPERIENCE LEVEL]
Tools and systems used: [TOOLS]
Raw notes, transcript or description of how it's done today: [NOTES]

Write the SOP with:
1. Purpose (one sentence) and when to use it.
2. Before you start — access, files and information needed.
3. Numbered steps. Each step starts with a verb, has one action, and names the tool or screen. Add sub-steps where needed.
4. Quality checks — how to know each key step was done right.
5. Common mistakes and how to fix them.
6. Who to contact if something goes wrong.
7. Owner and review date placeholders.

Keep wording simple. If my notes skip a step or are unclear, add a {QUESTION} marker in that spot instead of guessing.

## Speech or toast for a special occasion

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/special-occasion-speech-toast/
Category: Writing
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Write a warm, personal speech or toast for a wedding, birthday, retirement or farewell, timed to your length and full of real stories.

Prompt:

You are a speechwriter. Write a speech for me.

Occasion: [E.G. BEST MAN SPEECH, RETIREMENT, 60TH BIRTHDAY]
Person or people it's about: [NAMES AND RELATIONSHIP TO ME]
2–3 true stories or memories: [STORIES]
Qualities I want to highlight: [QUALITIES]
Audience: [WHO WILL BE THERE]
Tone: [E.G. FUNNY BUT HEARTFELT]
Length: [MINUTES]

Write:
1. An opening that introduces me and my connection in 1–2 sentences.
2. The stories, each linked to a quality.
3. A sincere middle section about what this person means to others.
4. A closing and a toast line.

Then give me: estimated speaking time, 3 places to pause, and a list of anything that might embarrass someone or exclude part of the audience.
Natural spoken language, short sentences, no clichéd quotes.

## Stop-motion style product animation prompt

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/stop-motion-product-animation/
Category: Video
Works with: Kling, Runway, Veo and Seedance
Published: 2026-11-20

Create a playful stop-motion style clip where your product and props move frame by frame on a colourful set, for social media ads.

Prompt:

Stop-motion animation style video, 12 frames per second look with slightly choppy, handmade movement.
Set: [SET, E.G. A PASTEL PINK TABLETOP WITH A PAPER BACKDROP].
Product: [PRODUCT].
Action: [SEQUENCE, E.G. THE BOX OPENS BY ITSELF, THE PRODUCT HOPS OUT, SMALL PROPS ARRANGE AROUND IT IN A CIRCLE].
Props: [PROPS, E.G. FRUIT SLICES, PAPER FLOWERS, SMALL WOODEN BLOCKS].
Camera: static top-down or straight-on view, no camera movement.
Lighting: bright, even, soft shadows. Colours: [PALETTE]. Playful, cheerful mood. Duration 6–8 seconds, no text, no hands visible. Aspect ratio [RATIO].

## Structured interview questions with a scorecard

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/structured-interview-scorecard/
Category: HR
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Create role-specific interview questions tied to the skills that matter, with what good answers sound like and a 1–5 scoring guide.

Prompt:

You are an experienced recruiter. Build a structured interview for this role.

Role and level: [ROLE AND SENIORITY]
Team and context: [TEAM CONTEXT]
4–6 must-have competencies or skills: [COMPETENCIES]
Common challenges in the first 6 months: [CHALLENGES]
Interview length: [MINUTES]

Create:
1. For each competency, 2 questions: one behavioural ("Tell me about a time…") and one situational ("What would you do if…").
2. For each question, 2 follow-up probes.
3. A scoring guide for each competency: what a 1, 3 and 5 answer sounds like.

## Supplier negotiation plan and email

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/supplier-negotiation-plan/
Category: Strategy
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Prepare for a supplier negotiation with your goals, walk-away point, trade-offs to offer and a clear opening email asking for better terms.

Prompt:

You are a procurement advisor. Help me prepare a supplier negotiation.

What I buy from them and annual spend: [PRODUCTS AND SPEND]
Relationship history (years, issues, reliability): [HISTORY]
What I want to improve: [GOALS, E.G. PRICE, PAYMENT TERMS, MINIMUM ORDER]
Alternatives I have (other suppliers, quotes): [ALTERNATIVES]
What I can offer in return: [E.G. LONGER CONTRACT, LARGER ORDERS, FASTER PAYMENT]

Create:
1. My goals in priority order, with an ideal outcome, a realistic target and a walk-away point for each.
2. My strengths and weaknesses in this negotiation.
3. Trade-offs to offer, ordered from cheapest for me to most costly.
4. Likely supplier objections and calm responses.
5. An opening email under 150 words that values the relationship and requests a conversation about specific terms.
6. A short checklist for the call itself, including what to confirm in writing afterwards.

Be realistic and fair — the goal is a deal both sides can keep.

## Survey results summary with key insights

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/survey-results-insights-summary/
Category: Research
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Turn raw survey responses into a clear summary of key findings, segment differences, themes from open answers and recommended actions.

Prompt:

You are a research analyst. Summarise these survey results.

Survey goal: [GOAL]
Who responded and how many: [RESPONDENTS]
Questions and results (counts or percentages per answer): [CLOSED QUESTION RESULTS]
Open-ended answers: [OPEN ANSWERS]
Segments to compare (e.g. new vs. long-time customers): [SEGMENTS]

Deliver:
1. 5–7 key findings, each with the supporting numbers and what it means.
2. Differences between segments, but only where the data shows a clear gap; note small sample sizes.
3. Themes from open answers: theme name, how many mentions, 2 representative quotes.
4. Surprises or contradictions in the data.
5. 3–5 recommended actions linked to specific findings.
6. Limitations of the survey (sample, wording, bias).
7. A 5-sentence executive summary.

Use only the data provided. Don't present differences as significant without enough responses to support them.

## Unit economics check with CAC, LTV and payback

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/unit-economics-cac-ltv/
Category: Finance
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-20

Calculate customer acquisition cost, lifetime value, LTV to CAC ratio and payback period from your numbers, with what to improve first.

Prompt:

You are a finance advisor for small and growing businesses. Analyse my unit economics.

Business model: [E.G. SUBSCRIPTION, ECOMMERCE, SERVICES]
Monthly marketing and sales spend: [SPEND]
New customers per month: [NEW CUSTOMERS]
Average revenue per customer per month (or per order and orders per year): [REVENUE]
Gross margin %: [MARGIN]
Monthly churn % or average customer lifetime: [CHURN OR LIFETIME]

Do this:
1. Calculate CAC, monthly gross profit per customer, LTV (gross-margin based), LTV:CAC ratio and CAC payback in months. Show each formula and the numbers you plugged in.
2. Explain in plain words what each result means for my business.
3. Run a sensitivity table: what happens to LTV:CAC if churn, CAC or price each improves by 10% and 20%.
4. Name the single lever with the biggest effect and 3 practical ways to improve it.
5. List any input that looks unusual or that I should double-check.

Do the arithmetic carefully. If an input is missing, state the assumption you used.

## Compare tools or vendors with a scoring matrix

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/vendor-comparison-scoring-matrix/

Published: 2026-11-20

Prompt:

Team size and users: [USERS]
Budget: [BUDGET]
Must-have requirements: [MUST-HAVES]
Nice-to-have requirements: [NICE-TO-HAVES]
Options and what I know about each (pricing, features, reviews, demo notes): [OPTIONS AND NOTES]

Do this:
1. Turn my requirements into 8–12 criteria with weights adding up to 100%. Explain the weights.

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/budget-from-bank-statement/

Fixed commitments I can't change soon: [RENT, LOANS, ETC.]

Provide:
1. A 5-sentence summary of what this contract does.
2. Key terms table: parties, start and end dates, payment amounts and timing, renewal, termination notice.
3. My obligations and the other party's obligations, as bullet lists.
4. Deadlines and dates I must remember.
5. Clauses that may be risky or unusual for someone in my role (e.g. automatic renewal, unlimited liability, broad non-compete, IP ownership, penalties), quoting the clause number and explaining why.
6. Questions to ask or changes to request before signing.

Quote the contract when you refer to it. If something is unclear or missing, say so instead of assuming.

## Turn customer interview notes into insights

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/customer-interview-synthesis/
Category: Research
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-19

Synthesise several customer interview transcripts into themes, supporting quotes, opportunities and a clear list of what to do next.

Prompt:

You are a user research lead. Synthesise these customer interviews.

Research goal: [WHAT WE WANTED TO LEARN]
Interviews (label each P1, P2, …; remove names):
[PASTE TRANSCRIPTS OR NOTES]

Deliver:
1. Key themes: for each, a one-line insight, how many participants mentioned it (e.g. 4 of 7), and 2–3 supporting quotes with participant labels.
2. Surprises: anything that contradicted our assumptions.
3. Differences between participant types, if any.
4. Opportunities: "How might we…" statements linked to the themes.
5. Recommended next steps, ranked by evidence strength and effort.
6. Gaps: questions the interviews didn't answer.

Separate what participants said from your interpretation. Don't treat one person's comment as a pattern.

## Customer pain points from real reviews

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/customer-pain-points-from-reviews/
Category: Marketing

Published: 2026-11-19

Paste reviews or support tickets and get a ranked map of customer pain points, with the exact phrases to reuse in your copy.

Prompt:

Product category: [PRODUCT CATEGORY]
Source of reviews: [E.G. MY PRODUCT, COMPETITOR X, AMAZON, G2, APP STORE]

Reviews:
[PASTE 20–200 REVIEWS OR TICKETS]

Output:
1. A table of pain points with columns: pain point, how often it appears (count), severity (1–5), 2–3 exact customer quotes.
2. Sort by count × severity, highest first.
3. Desired outcomes: what customers say they wanted instead, in their own words.

## Customer persona built from real interviews

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/customer-persona-from-interviews/
Category: Strategy
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-19

Turn interview notes or survey answers into an evidence-based customer persona with goals, frustrations, buying triggers and quotes.

Prompt:

You are a customer research lead. Build a customer persona from the research below.

Product: [WHAT YOU SELL]
Research notes (interviews, surveys, sales calls — remove names):
[PASTE NOTES]

Create a persona with:
1. A short descriptive name (role-based, e.g. "The overloaded ops manager") and a one-line summary.
2. Context: role, situation, tools they use today.
3. Goals: what they are trying to achieve, in priority order.
4. Frustrations: what gets in the way, with supporting quotes.
5. Buying triggers: events that make them look for a solution.
6. Decision process: who else is involved, what they compare, what makes them hesitate.
7. Words they use to describe the problem (for marketing copy).
8. How to reach them: channels and content they mention.

Every point must be backed by the notes. List open questions where the evidence is thin.
If the notes clearly show two different types of customer, create two personas instead of blending them.

## Debug an error without guesswork

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/debug-error-step-by-step/
Category: Coding
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-19

Make the AI find the real cause of a bug from your error and code, list its assumptions and suggest a minimal fix instead of guessing.

Prompt:

You are a senior [LANGUAGE/FRAMEWORK] developer helping me debug. Work from evidence only.

What I expected: [EXPECTED BEHAVIOUR]
What happens instead: [ACTUAL BEHAVIOUR]
Full error message and stack trace:
[PASTE ERROR]
Relevant code:
[PASTE CODE]
Environment: [VERSIONS, OS, RUNTIME]
What I already tried: [ATTEMPTS]

Rules:
1. First, explain in plain words what the error means.
2. List the 2–3 most likely causes, ranked, and for each point to the exact line or evidence that supports it.
3. If you need to see another file, a config or a log to be sure, ask for it instead of guessing.
4. Suggest the smallest change that fixes the most likely cause, as a diff.
5. Tell me how to confirm the fix worked and how to prevent the bug from coming back (a test or a check).
Do not invent functions, APIs or library options. If you are unsure whether something exists in my version, say so.

## Explain any concept with everyday analogies

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/explain-with-everyday-analogies/
Category: Education
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-19

Understand a hard idea through three everyday analogies, a plain definition, a worked example and a quick self-check quiz.

Prompt:

Explain [CONCEPT] to me. My background: [WHAT YOU ALREADY KNOW, E.G. "HIGH SCHOOL MATHS" OR "NO TECHNICAL BACKGROUND"].

Structure:
1. One-sentence plain definition with no jargon.
2. Three analogies from everyday life ([OPTIONAL: TOPICS I LIKE, E.G. COOKING, FOOTBALL]). For each, say in one line where the analogy stops being accurate.
3. A worked example with real numbers or a concrete case.
4. The 3 most common misunderstandings about this concept.
5. A 5-question quiz (mix multiple choice and short answer). Put the answers at the very end.

Keep it under 500 words before the quiz.

Proof I can honestly use: [REVIEWS COUNT, RATINGS, AWARDS, GUARANTEE OR NONE]
Destination: [LANDING PAGE OR PRODUCT PAGE]

Write 5 ad variants, each with a different angle:
1. Pain — the problem they face now
2. Outcome — life after using the product
3. Objection — answers the main reason people don't buy
4. How it works — simple and concrete

## Follow-up emails when a prospect goes quiet

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/follow-up-email-no-reply/

Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-19

Prompt:

Prospect: [NAME, ROLE, COMPANY]
What they cared about: [THEIR GOALS OR PROBLEMS]
Useful things I can share: [ARTICLE, CASE STUDY, IDEA, TEMPLATE, NEWS ABOUT THEIR INDUSTRY]

## Design pricing tiers customers understand

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/pricing-tiers-strategy/
Category: Strategy
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-19

Plan good-better-best pricing tiers based on customer segments and value, with clear feature splits and the risks of each option.

Prompt:

You are a pricing strategist. Help me design pricing tiers.

Product: [PRODUCT AND MAIN FEATURES]
Customer segments: [SEGMENTS, WITH WHAT EACH VALUES MOST]
Current pricing (if any): [CURRENT PRICES]
Competitor prices I know: [COMPETITOR PRICING]
Costs per customer: [ROUGH COSTS]
Business goal: [MORE CUSTOMERS, HIGHER REVENUE PER CUSTOMER, MOVE UPMARKET]

Deliver:
1. The value metric: what customers should pay more for (seats, usage, projects, locations) and why it fits.
2. Three tiers (entry, core, premium): target segment, price range, included features, limits. Explain why someone would upgrade.
3. Which tier should be the one most customers choose, and how the page design can make that clear.
4. Risks: features that might cannibalise upgrades, prices that might hurt margin.
5. A simple test plan: what to test first and what result would tell me to change.

Show your reasoning. Treat all prices as starting points to test, not final answers.

## Design a survey that gets honest answers

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/survey-questionnaire-design/
Category: Research
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-19

Create a short, unbiased survey for customers or users, with clear question types, logical order and a plan for analysing the answers.

Prompt:

You are a survey research specialist. Design a survey.

Purpose: [WHAT DECISION THE RESULTS WILL INFORM]
Audience: [WHO WILL ANSWER AND HOW YOU WILL REACH THEM]
Max time to complete: [MINUTES]
Topics I want to cover: [TOPICS]

Create:
1. 3–5 research questions the survey must answer.
2. The survey: 8–15 questions in a logical order (easy first, sensitive last). For each give question text, type (multiple choice, scale, ranking, open text), answer options and which research question it serves.
3. One screening question if needed.
4. A short intro text explaining purpose, time and privacy.
5. A bias check: point out any question that could be leading, double-barrelled or confusing, and fix it.
6. How to analyse the results: what to count, compare or segment.

Keep scales consistent (e.g. all 1–5 with labelled ends) and always include "Other" or "Not sure" where it fits.

## SWOT analysis that leads to actions

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/swot-analysis-with-actions/
Category: Strategy
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-19

Build a SWOT analysis from your own facts, then turn it into prioritised strategic actions with owners, using the TOWS matrix.

Prompt:

You are a strategy consultant. Run a SWOT analysis for my business and turn it into actions.

Business: [WHAT IT DOES, SIZE, MARKET]
Goal for the next 12 months: [GOAL]
Facts I know: [SALES TRENDS, CUSTOMER FEEDBACK, TEAM, FINANCES, COMPETITORS, MARKET CHANGES]

Steps:
1. SWOT: 4–6 points per box. Strengths and weaknesses are internal; opportunities and threats are external. Base each point on my facts and mark assumptions.
2. TOWS matrix:
   - SO: use strengths to capture opportunities
   - WO: fix weaknesses to capture opportunities
   - ST: use strengths to reduce threats
   - WT: reduce weaknesses to avoid threats
   Give 2 strategies for each.
3. Choose the 5 strategies most likely to help reach my goal. For each: first action, owner role, cost level (low/medium/high), and how we'll measure progress.

Keep it concise; one line per point.

## Find your unique selling proposition

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/unique-selling-proposition-finder/
Category: Strategy

Published: 2026-11-19

Turn what you know about your product, customers and rivals into three sharp selling propositions you can test on a homepage or ad.

Prompt:

What I sell: [PRODUCT OR SERVICE]
Who buys it: [TARGET CUSTOMER]
Main alternatives customers consider: [COMPETITORS OR "DOING NOTHING"]
What customers praise most (reviews, emails, calls): [REAL CUSTOMER FEEDBACK]
Things we do that competitors don't: [DIFFERENCES, EVEN SMALL ONES]

Steps:

- Gains (outcomes they want), ranked by how much they matter

## Write unit tests that catch real bugs

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/write-unit-tests/
Category: Coding
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-19

Generate focused unit tests for a function, covering normal cases, edge cases and errors, in your test framework and project style.

Prompt:

You are a senior engineer who writes careful tests. Write unit tests for the code below.

Language and test framework: [E.G. PYTHON + PYTEST, TYPESCRIPT + VITEST, JAVA + JUNIT]
Code to test:
[PASTE FUNCTION OR CLASS]
What it is supposed to do: [EXPECTED BEHAVIOUR, BUSINESS RULES]
Example of an existing test in my project (for style): [PASTE OR "NONE"]

Steps:
1. Test plan: list cases grouped as normal, edge (empty, zero, max, unicode, boundaries, time zones), and error cases.
2. Write the tests. One behaviour per test, descriptive names, arrange-act-assert layout.

4. List any behaviour in the code that seems to contradict the expected behaviour — likely bugs.
5. Note anything that would be hard to test and suggest a small refactor.

Use only APIs that exist in my framework version. Don't change the code under test unless I ask.

## YouTube video script with a strong hook

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/youtube-video-script/
Category: Marketing
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-19

Write a YouTube script with a 15-second hook, clear sections, pattern breaks to hold attention and a natural call to action.

Prompt:

You are a YouTube scriptwriter. Write a script for my video.

Video title: [TITLE]
Channel topic and audience: [WHO WATCHES]
Video length: [MINUTES]
Key points to cover: [POINTS]
My style: [E.G. CALM TEACHER, FAST AND FUNNY, STORY-DRIVEN]
Call to action: [SUBSCRIBE, WATCH NEXT VIDEO, LINK IN DESCRIPTION]

Structure:

## Cold email that gets replies

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/cold-email-that-gets-replies/
Category: Writing
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-18

Turn a few facts about your offer and your prospect into a short, specific cold email — plus two follow-ups.

Prompt:

You are an experienced B2B copywriter who writes short cold emails with high reply rates.

Write a cold email from me to a prospect.

About me and my offer:
- My name and role: [YOUR NAME, ROLE]
- Company: [YOUR COMPANY]
- What we do, in one sentence: [YOUR OFFER]
- One concrete result we got for a client: [RESULT WITH A NUMBER]

About the prospect:
- Name and role: [PROSPECT NAME, ROLE]
- Company: [PROSPECT COMPANY]
- Something specific I noticed about them: [RECENT NEWS, POST OR PROBLEM]

Rules:
1. Maximum 90 words in the body.
2. The first line must be about the prospect, not about me.

7. Plain text, friendly and direct.

- 3 subject line options (under 6 words each)
- The email
- 2 short follow-ups (under 50 words each) to send 3 and 7 days later, each adding a new angle instead of "just bumping this"

## Gemini photo editing prompt

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/gemini-photo-editing/
Category: Image
Works with: Gemini and ChatGPT
Published: 2026-11-18

Edit your own photo with Gemini using plain language — change the background, light or style while keeping the person or product exactly the same.

Prompt:

Edit the photo I uploaded.

Keep exactly the same: [WHAT MUST NOT CHANGE, E.G. "MY FACE, HAIR, EXPRESSION AND CLOTHES"]

Change:
- Background: [NEW BACKGROUND, E.G. "A BRIGHT MINIMAL OFFICE WITH SOFT DAYLIGHT"]
- Lighting: [E.G. "SOFT, EVEN LIGHT FROM THE LEFT"]
- Style: [E.G. "NATURAL, REALISTIC PHOTO, NOT ILLUSTRATED"]
- Framing: [E.G. "HEAD AND SHOULDERS, SQUARE CROP"]

Make the result look like one real photo: matching shadows, natural skin texture, no smoothing, no extra people or objects, no text.

## LinkedIn post from a real experience

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/linkedin-post-from-experience/
Category: Marketing
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-18

Turn something that happened at work into a LinkedIn post with a strong first line, one clear lesson and no cringe.

Prompt:

Help me write a LinkedIn post based on a real experience.

What happened (rough notes): [THE SITUATION, WHAT YOU DID, WHAT HAPPENED]
What I learned: [THE LESSON IN YOUR OWN WORDS]
Who I want to read it: [E.G. "STARTUP FOUNDERS", "JUNIOR DESIGNERS"]
My role: [YOUR JOB TITLE OR FIELD]

Write 3 versions:
A. Story first: start in the middle of the moment.
B. Lesson first: start with the takeaway, then the story that proves it.
C. Contrarian: start with a common belief this experience challenges.

Rules for every version:
- First line under 12 words and specific enough to make someone stop scrolling.
- Short paragraphs of 1–2 sentences.
- 120–200 words.
- One clear lesson, not five.
- End with a question that invites people to share their own experience.
- No buzzwords ("excited to announce", "humbled", "game-changer"), no fake cliffhangers, no more than 3 hashtags.
- Do not add details that are not in my notes.

## Make ChatGPT write like a human

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/make-chatgpt-write-like-a-human/
Category: Writing
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-18

A prompt that rewrites stiff AI text so it sounds like a real person wrote it — plainer words, varied rhythm, no filler.

Prompt:

Rewrite the text below so it sounds like it was written by a real person, not an AI.

Who is writing it: [WHO YOU ARE, E.G. "A FREELANCE DESIGNER"]
Who will read it: [AUDIENCE]
Tone: [E.G. "FRIENDLY AND DIRECT", "CALM AND PROFESSIONAL"]

Do:
- Use plain, everyday words. If a simpler word works, use it.
- Mix short and long sentences. A few very short ones are fine.
- Keep concrete details and numbers; cut vague claims.
- Write the way this person would explain it out loud.
- Keep the meaning and all facts exactly the same.

Do not:
- Use these words: delve, elevate, leverage, seamless, robust, unlock, tapestry, landscape, game-changer, in today's fast-paced world.
- Start with "In conclusion", "Overall" or "Ultimately", or end paragraphs with a summary line.
- Use more than one dash per paragraph or any emojis.
- Add new facts, opinions or examples that are not in the original.

Return only the rewritten text. Then, under a line, list the 3 biggest changes you made.

Text:
[PASTE YOUR TEXT]

Category: Image
Works with: Midjourney, Ideogram and Flux
Published: 2026-11-18

A Midjourney prompt for clean, simple logo concepts — flat vector style, one idea, plain background — to explore before a designer finalises it.

Minimal flat vector logo for [BRAND NAME], a [WHAT THE BUSINESS DOES]. A single simple symbol of [ONE CONCEPT, E.G. "A LEAF FORMED FROM TWO OVERLAPPING CIRCLES"], [STYLE, E.G. "GEOMETRIC, BOLD LINES"], [1–2 COLOURS, E.G. "DEEP GREEN ON WHITE"]. Centred on a plain white background, lots of empty space, no gradients, no shadows, no mockup, no extra text, clean professional brand mark, simple enough to work at small sizes.

## Resume bullet points that show results

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/resume-bullet-points-with-results/
Category: Careers
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-18

Turn a list of job duties into strong resume bullet points built on action, scope and result — tuned to the role you want.

Prompt:

Act as a professional resume writer. Rewrite my experience into strong resume bullet points.

Target role: [THE JOB TITLE YOU ARE APPLYING FOR]
My current or past role: [JOB TITLE, COMPANY TYPE, YEARS]
What I did there (duties, projects, wins — rough notes are fine):
[PASTE YOUR NOTES]

Rules for each bullet:
- Format: strong action verb + what I did + scale or scope + result.
- One line, maximum 25 words.
- Start every bullet with a different verb. Avoid "responsible for", "helped", "worked on".
- Use numbers only if I gave them. Where a number would help but is missing, put {ADD NUMBER} so I can fill it in.
- Prioritise what is most relevant to the target role.

Give me:
1. 5–7 bullets for this role, ordered from most to least relevant to the target role.
2. A list of questions about numbers or results I should find out to make the bullets stronger.
3. 10 keywords from the target role that should appear somewhere in my resume.

## SEO content brief for any keyword

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/seo-content-brief/
Category: SEO
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-18

Get a complete SEO content brief — search intent, outline, questions to answer and internal links — before you write a single word.

Prompt:

You are an SEO content strategist. Create a content brief for an article.

Target keyword: [MAIN KEYWORD]
Secondary keywords (optional): [OTHER KEYWORDS, OR "SUGGEST THEM"]
My website: [WHAT YOUR SITE IS ABOUT AND WHO IT SERVES]
My product or offer to mention naturally (optional): [OFFER]

Include:
1. Search intent: what the person typing this keyword wants, in one sentence, and what type of page fits best (guide, list, comparison, tool, template).
2. Title options: 3 titles under 60 characters, each including the main keyword.
3. Meta description: under 155 characters.
4. Outline: H2 and H3 headings in order, with 1–2 lines on what each section must say.
5. Questions to answer: 6 questions people ask about this topic, to cover in the text or an FAQ.
6. Unique angle: one thing this article can include that typical pages on this topic miss (a template, a worked example, a checklist, original data from my business).
7. Internal links: 3 types of pages on my site this article should link to.
8. Recommended length, with a reason.

Do not invent statistics. Where a number would help, write {FIND SOURCE}.

## AI video scene with dialogue and sound

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/veo-dialogue-scene/
Category: Video
Works with: Veo, Seedance and Kling
Published: 2026-11-18

A prompt for AI video models that generate audio — one short scene with a character, a spoken line, ambient sound and a clear camera plan.

Prompt:

8-second cinematic video, [ASPECT RATIO, E.G. "VERTICAL 9:16"], photorealistic.

Scene: [PLACE AND TIME, E.G. "A SMALL BAKERY AT DAWN, WARM LIGHT THROUGH THE WINDOW"]
Character: [WHO, E.G. "A WOMAN IN HER 30S WITH FLOUR ON HER APRON, CALM AND PROUD"]
Action: [WHAT SHE DOES, E.G. "SHE TAKES A TRAY OF BREAD OUT OF THE OVEN AND TURNS TO THE CAMERA"]

Camera: [E.G. "SLOW PUSH-IN FROM MEDIUM SHOT TO CLOSE-UP, STEADY, SHALLOW DEPTH OF FIELD"]

Dialogue: she says, warmly and clearly: "[ONE SHORT LINE, MAX 12 WORDS]"
Audio: [AMBIENT SOUND, E.G. "QUIET OVEN HUM, BIRDS OUTSIDE, NO MUSIC"]

Avoid: subtitles, on-screen text, extra people, distorted hands, sudden cuts.

## Landing page hero that explains itself in 5 seconds

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/landing-page-hero-copy/
Category: Marketing
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-17

Get 5 headline and subheadline pairs for your landing page, each built on a different angle, with a clear call to action.

Prompt:

Act as a conversion copywriter. Write hero sections for my landing page.

Product: [PRODUCT NAME]
What it does: [ONE SENTENCE]
Who it's for: [TARGET CUSTOMER]
The main problem it solves: [PROBLEM]
What makes it different from alternatives: [DIFFERENCE]
Proof I can mention (optional): [NUMBER OF USERS, RESULT, AWARD]

Write 5 hero versions. Each must use a different angle:
1. Outcome — the result the customer gets
2. Pain — the problem it removes
3. Speed or ease — how fast or simple it is
4. Contrast — compared with the old way of doing it
5. Proof — built around the strongest proof point

For each version give:
- Headline: maximum 8 words, no jargon
- Subheadline: one sentence, maximum 20 words, says what the product is and who it's for
- Button text: 2–4 words, starts with a verb, describes what happens on click
- One sentence on why this angle could work for my audience

Then tell me which version you would test first and why.

## Pre-mortem for any plan

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/pre-mortem-for-any-plan/
Category: Strategy
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-16

Ask the AI to imagine your plan has already failed, then work backwards to find the risks you haven't seen yet.

Prompt:

I want to run a pre-mortem on a plan. Be direct and specific; do not reassure me.

The plan: [DESCRIBE THE PLAN IN 3–6 SENTENCES]
Goal and deadline: [WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE, BY WHEN]
Resources: [BUDGET, TEAM, TIME]
What I'm already worried about: [YOUR CONCERNS, OR "NOTHING YET"]

Step 1. Imagine it is [DATE 12 MONTHS FROM NOW] and the plan has clearly failed. Write a short, realistic story (about 150 words) of how it failed.

Step 2. List the 8 most likely causes of failure. For each, give:
- Cause
- Early warning sign I could notice in the first month
- Likelihood (low / medium / high) and impact (low / medium / high)
- One concrete action to prevent it or reduce the damage

Step 3. Which assumption in my plan is the riskiest? Suggest the cheapest, fastest test I could run this week to check it.

Step 4. Ask me 3 questions you would need answered to improve this analysis.

## Learn any topic in 7 days

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/learn-anything-in-a-week/
Category: Productivity
Works with: ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-15

Get a 7-day study plan with daily goals, practice tasks and quick self-tests — tuned to your level and the time you have.

Prompt:

Act as an expert tutor in [TOPIC].

My current level: [NONE / BEGINNER / SOME EXPERIENCE — DESCRIBE]
Why I want to learn it: [YOUR GOAL, E.G. "BUILD A SIMPLE BUDGET MODEL IN EXCEL"]
Time I have: [MINUTES PER DAY] minutes a day for 7 days

Create a 7-day plan. For each day give:
- Goal: one sentence, what I'll be able to do by the end of the day
- Learn (about 30% of the time): the key concepts, explained simply, with one example each
- Practice (about 60%): a concrete exercise I can do with free tools
- Check (about 10%): 3 quick questions to test myself, with answers hidden at the end of the day's section

Rules:
- Use the 20% of the topic that gives 80% of the practical results.
- Each day builds on the previous one.
- Day 7 is a small final project that uses everything.
- Point out the 3 most common beginner mistakes and when they usually happen.

After the plan, wait. When I write "Day 1 done", quiz me on day 1 before moving on.

## Senior-level code review

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/senior-code-review/
Category: Coding
Works with: Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini
Published: 2026-11-14

Get a structured code review that ranks problems by severity — bugs and security first, style last — with concrete fixes.

Prompt:

You are a senior [LANGUAGE / FRAMEWORK] engineer doing a code review.

Context:
- What this code does: [SHORT DESCRIPTION]
- Where it runs: [E.G. "PUBLIC API, ~1000 REQUESTS/MIN" OR "INTERNAL SCRIPT"]
- What I'm most unsure about: [YOUR CONCERN, OR "NOTHING SPECIFIC"]

Review the code below. Group findings by severity:

1. Critical — bugs, data loss, security issues, race conditions
2. Important — error handling, edge cases, performance problems at the stated scale
3. Maintainability — unclear names, duplication, missing tests for risky logic
4. Minor — style and small improvements (maximum 5)

For each finding:
- Quote the line(s)
- Explain the problem in 1–2 sentences, with an input or scenario that triggers it
- Show the fixed code

Do not invent problems to fill a category; write "None found" if it's clean.
End with: the single most important change to make first.

Code:
[PASTE YOUR CODE]

Professional studio product photograph of [PRODUCT, WITH COLOUR AND MATERIAL], placed on [SURFACE, E.G. "A SLAB OF WARM TRAVERTINE"], [BACKGROUND, E.G. "SOFT BEIGE SEAMLESS BACKDROP"]. Soft diffused key light from the left, gentle rim light separating the product from the background, subtle realistic shadow. [PROP, E.G. "A SPRIG OF DRIED EUCALYPTUS"] slightly out of focus at the edge of the frame. ## Cinematic 8-second product reveal

URL: https://goodaipromt.com/prompts/cinematic-product-reveal-video/
Category: Video
Works with: Seedance, Veo, Kling and Runway
Published: 2026-11-12

A shot-by-shot prompt for AI video models that turns a product into a short, cinematic reveal for ads and Reels.

Prompt:

Cinematic product reveal, 8 seconds, vertical 9:16, photorealistic.

Product: [PRODUCT, WITH COLOUR, MATERIAL AND SIZE]
Setting: [SETTING, E.G. "DARK STUDIO WITH A GLOSSY BLACK FLOOR"]
Mood and colour palette: [MOOD, E.G. "LUXURY, DEEP BLUE AND GOLD ACCENTS"]

0–2 s: Darkness. A thin line of light slowly sweeps across the frame, revealing the edge of the product in silhouette. Slow push-in.
2–5 s: The camera arcs smoothly around the product at the same height. Light reflections glide across its surface, showing texture and material. [DETAIL TO SHOW, E.G. "WATER DROPLETS ON THE BOTTLE"]
5–8 s: The camera settles into a clean front-facing hero shot. The light fully comes up. The product stands still in the centre, with empty space above it for a title.

Camera: smooth, stabilised, no shake, no fast cuts. Shallow depth of field.
Avoid: text, logos, hands, extra objects, warping or changes to the product's shape.
